articles.title: Sandiganbayan drops graft, plunder charges vs Bonoan
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division has dropped the plunder and graft charges against former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan, removing him as an accused in two cases linked to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division has dropped the plunder and graft charges against former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan, removing him as an accused in two cases linked to an alleged P573-million kickback scheme.
“He (Bonoan) is no longer an accused in the two cases before the Fifth [Division],” a member of the prosecution team told the Inquirer on Tuesday.
Another source confirmed the development.

Also accused in those cases are Sen. Jose “Jinggoy” Estrada, Department Of Public Works And Highways (DPWH) district engineers Manny Bulusan and Arturo Gonzales Jr., and assistant district engineer Denryl Caesar Cortuna.
The source from the prosecution said the other accused may be expected to file a motion for reconsideration.

The latest Sandiganbayan action came after the Office of the Ombudsman pursued efforts beginning in July to turn Bonoan into a state witness for other cases stemming from alleged multibillion-peso corruption involving flood control projects.
Flood control probe
Bonoan resigned as DPWH secretary in September 2025, shortly after President Marcos ordered an investigation into the alleged anomalies.
In November 2025, the now-defunct Independent Commission for Infrastructure found Bonoan administratively liable over flood control projects in Bulacan province that were supposedly never built.
The Department of Justice said in January that Bonoan would also face a criminal case for plunder.

Bonoan earlier testified before the antigraft court in a separate case against former Sen. Ramon “Bong” Revilla Jr. over a P76.91-million flood control project in Pandi, Bulacan, that prosecutors said proved “nonexistent.”
At one point in his testimony, Bonoan said “all senators” who were incumbent in 2024 availed themselves of a “leadership fund” allotted by the DPWH under the 2025 budget. /cb

articles.title: Most cybercrimes still tied to SIM cards despite law – PNP
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police-Anti-Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG) has pushed for amendments to the SIM Card Registration Act, saying that despite its passage, almost all recent…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police-Anti-Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG) has pushed for amendments to the SIM Card Registration Act, saying that despite its passage, almost all recent cybercrime cases in the country still involve subscriber identity modules (SIM) cards.

PNP-ACG director Maj. Gen. Wilson Casil Asueta made the suggestion during a press briefing on Tuesday after reporting that authorities arrested a 26-year-old man in Obando, Bulacan, on Aug. 24 for the illegal sale of around 400 registered SIM cards.

“Our SIM Card Registration Act is not being implemented effectively. We need new provisions so we are appealing to our legislators for the immediate passage of amended laws for this purpose,” Asueta said.
According to him, cyberspace crimes involving SIM cards include scamming, online gambling and identity exploitation.

“I can honestly say that almost all cybercrimes committed start with SIM cards. That is our problem. It is difficult for us to monitor because there are so many lacking provisions and our laws, including the SIM Card Registration Act, are no longer applicable,” Asueta said.
Among the amendments being proposed by the PNP-ACG are identity authentication and the activation of SIM cards only after successful authentication and registration.
Preferred ID
“If possible, we should only use one ID, our national ID which comes with biometric information,” Asueta said.
He also suggested limiting SIM card ownership to a maximum of five per person and monitoring the distribution and redistribution of SIM cards.

President Marcos signed the SIM Card Registration Act, or Republic Act No. 11934, in 2022 to provide “accountability in the use of SIM cards and aid law enforcers in tracking perpetrators of crimes committed through phones.”
RA 11934 was also aimed at “significantly boosting government initiatives against scams committed through text and online messages.”
Under the law, telco companies and direct sellers must ask for a valid ID from SIM card buyers.
Those who already owned a SIM card before RA 11934 took effect were also required to register the card with telcos within a certain period or else, it would be deactivated.
Penalties were also listed for those who registered a SIM card using false or fake information, as well as those who used the SIM card for illegal activities. /cb

articles.title: Ang: NLEx flooding due to blocked dam water
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — San Miguel Corp. (SMC) president Ramon Ang attributed the flooding along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEx) to soil and debris left behind during the 2024 repair of the NLEx…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — San Miguel Corp. (SMC) president Ramon Ang attributed the flooding along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEx) to soil and debris left behind during the 2024 repair of the NLEx Tulaoc Bridge.

Speaking to Bulacan journalists on Tuesday, Ang said the debris had obstructed the flow of water released from Pantabangan Dam in Nueva Ecija, which cascaded through Pampanga before emptying into Manila Bay.
“The soil had blocked the waterways. They just left it there. They have to remove it to clear the waterways,” he said.
Ang offered to help NLEx address the flooding, which caused up to eight hours of traffic congestion on Monday.

Ang is set to serve as chief executive officer of the planned “mega tollway” company that will be formed through the merger of the country’s two largest toll road operators, Metro Pacific Tollways Corp. (MPTC) and SMC.
MPTC operates NLEx, while SMC operates the South Luzon Expressway and other major toll roads.
The planned merger is expected to create a larger tollway operator with a wider network of expressways across Luzon.
Broader drainage problem

In a statement, MPTC assured motorists that it would continue working with national and local agencies to speed up flood-prevention measures and restore reliable travel along the affected NLEx corridor.
The company said it was closely coordinating with the Department of Transportation, Toll Regulatory Board, and other government agencies to assess immediate measures to assist motorists.
MPTC said it would raise the northbound and southbound pavements in Tulaoc, San Simon, Pampanga, once the Tulaoc Bridge elevation was completed.

MPTC cited Pampanga Gov. Lilia Pineda’s statement that the flooding reflected a broader drainage problem in the province, with water backing up because downstream areas such as Macabebe and Masantol were already saturated and floodwaters could not readily drain into Manila Bay.
MPTC likewise cited Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon’s observation that the sheer volume of water brought by the southwest monsoon had overwhelmed the drainage system. /cb

articles.title: Stuck on NLEx: ‘As if we went abroad’
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — These detours are not the happy kind. Several netizens shared their experiences of driving for hours over the weekend due to heavy traffic along the North Luzon Expressway…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — These detours are not the happy kind.
Several netizens shared their experiences of driving for hours over the weekend due to heavy traffic along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEx), amid flooding brought by days of torrential rains.
Many towns in Pampanga province, which the NLEx runs through, were inundated as the southwest monsoon (“habagat”) lashed parts of Luzon.

In a post shared with the Facebook group “Traffic Updates—NLEx / SCTEx / TPLEx,” a social media user said she left La Union around 6:30 a.m. on Monday, Aug. 31, and arrived in Taguig City only at 4:30 a.m. on Tuesday, Sept. 1—or 22 hours later.
The heavy traffic along portions of NLEx forced her to take detours through the towns of Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, and Bulacan.
“Parang nag-abroad lang e” (It was as if we went abroad), she said.
SCTEx refers to the Subic-Clark-Tarlac Expressway, while TPLEx refers to the Tarlac-Pangasinan-La Union Expressway.
“We managed to take a staycation in many different provinces and places… Imagine, we got around! We were even greeted by Jose Mari Chan on the road!,” the user quipped in Filipino.
Chan is a beloved figure in Philippine music, best known for his Christmas carols that are often used to signal the start of the Yuletide season as early as September.

Another social media user said she and her family left their flooded home in Apalit town, Pampanga, at 9 a.m. on Monday, and managed to arrive at a relative’s home in Dau, in the same province, at 5 a.m. on Tuesday.
Impassable roads

The netizen said roads going through Apalit, San Simon, and San Fernando were impassable due to waist-deep floods at the time. They had gone to Calumpit, Bulacan, in hopes of catching a big bus to pass through the flooded areas, but there was no bus.
However, a truck driver allowed them to board his vehicle until NLEx, where the vehicle could no longer bear the weight of the passengers.

“IT WAS A TRUCK FOR COWS. Not a bus, not rescue trucks from the government. But, thank you to the driver who still tried to help us,” the netizen said, adding, “I hope the government still has some mercy for us.”
Still another social media user said they left Dinalupihan, Bataan, at 4 p.m. on Monday and arrived in Santa Rosa, Laguna, at 8:30 a.m. on Tuesday.
They were likewise forced to take detours through several towns in Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, and Bulacan before finding their way to their destination.
Because of their ordeal, she said, one is forced to wonder where the people’s taxes go.
‘Deeply sorry’
In a statement on Monday, NLEx operator Metro Pacific Tollways Corp. (MPTC) said it understood the public’s frustration and that it was “deeply sorry” for the delays the motorists endured.
MPTC said concrete barriers will be deployed along the Tulaoc Bridge in San Simon, Pampanga, to serve as a temporary flood wall, as well as siphoning trucks to remove the floodwater.

In an advisory on Tuesday morning, NLEX Corp. said heavy traffic was still reported on both the northbound and southbound lanes of the expressway segment near San Simon, but that all types of vehicles could pass through the Lane 1 segment.
However, only Class 2 and 3 vehicles, or larger vehicles including buses and trucks, could use the Lane 2 segment.
‘Why still go there?’
Malacañang on Tuesday, meanwhile, advised motorists to avoid NLEx for now, following reports of motorists getting stranded on the expressway due to severe flooding.
At a briefing, Palace press officer Claire Castro dismissed proposals to temporarily suspend NLEx toll fees, saying doing so could result in heavier traffic.
“Why are you still going in if there’s already traffic? Don’t use it for now if you won’t be able to get through anyway,” she said.
“What’s the point of making it (toll-) free? If we make it free, more vehicles will enter. And the more vehicles that enter, the worse the traffic will get,” Castro added.
Castro said there was no order from President Marcos to sanction NLEx operator MPTC, as the President was focused on finding ways to ease traffic congestion. /cb

articles.title: Army: No OVP, DepEd funds for youth programs
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Army received no money from the Office of the Vice President (OVP), the Department of Education (DepEd), or the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Army received no money from the Office of the Vice President (OVP), the Department of Education (DepEd), or the Vice Presidential Security and Protection Group (VPSPG) for two youth programs that DepEd later cited to justify P15.54 million in confidential fund spending, an Army officer testified on Tuesday.

Col. Manaros Boransing II, former assistant chief of staff for civil-military operations of the Army’s 1st Infantry “Tabak” Division, told the Senate impeachment court that the division conducted the 2023 Youth Leadership Summit (YLS) and Information Education Campaign (IEC) using its own allocations.

“There was no funding released to the 1st Infantry Division from DepEd, Sir, of any source,” Boransing said under questioning by private prosecutor Reynaldo Robles on Day 20 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial.

Asked whether the OVP or VPSPG had provided confidential funds for the activities, Boransing reiterated: “For 2023, Sir, there were no funds from other any government agency released to the First Infantry Division.”
The programs were intended to prevent young people from being recruited by violent extremist groups, he said.

The testimony highlighted a disconnect between the Army’s account of the programs and DepEd documents that the prosecution says were used to support the liquidation of P15.54 million in confidential fund rewards in 2023.
Boransing said he issued certifications confirming the participation of DepEd and other stakeholders in the YLS and IEC after DepEd requested them.
But the certificates did not state that DepEd had spent money on the activities, much less confidential or intelligence funds, he said.
Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros asked whether his certification could be treated as proof that DepEd properly disbursed its confidential funds.
“No, Ma’am,” Boransing replied.
“The certification was [for] their (DepEd) and other stakeholders’ participation in the Youth Leadership Summit and the Information Education Communication Campaign.”
The certification contained no specific funds, expenditures or amounts, he said.
“There was no mention of any [DepEd] funds in the certification that we issued,” Boransing added.
He also said he had no personal knowledge of how DepEd paid for its participation.
“I don’t know how they paid for their expenses,” he said.
The prosecution has alleged that the Army certifications were among documents used by DepEd to support its claim that confidential funds were spent on rewards to informants.

Boransing said he did not know the certificates would later be used as liquidation documents for confidential fund spending. The documents were intended only to confirm that the activities took place and that participating agencies were present, he said.
There was no intelligence gathering during the summits, he added.
Col. Magtangol Panopio, another prosecution witness, likewise testified that he issued a certification that DepEd later used in liquidating confidential funds in 2024.
Panopio said he was unaware that his certification would be used to help liquidate P15.54 million in confidential-fund rewards.

“We were a little surprised because our certification is only for the certification that we conducted the Youth Leadership Summit. We did not certify anything about money or funds,” he told the court.
Army had funded programs
The YLS and IEC were Army-led initiatives conducted with DepEd and other government agencies.
Boransing’s testimony echoed statements he and other Army officials made during a 2024 House committee inquiry into the alleged misuse of P612.5 million in confidential funds under the OVP and DepEd.
Relevant portions of the House hearings were shown during Tuesday’s trial.

Army officials told the House panel that the Army and local governments had shouldered the costs of the activities and that they would not have issued certifications had they known DepEd would use them to justify confidential fund rewards.

Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro, now the lead public prosecutor in Duterte’s impeachment trial, noted during that inquiry that DepEd appeared to have claimed P15.54 million in confidential-fund spending for activities actually undertaken and funded by the Army and local governments.
Retired Education Undersecretary and Maj. Gen. Nolasco Mempin also confirmed that DepEd did not allocate funds for the YLS because it was an AFP program.
Prosecution lawyer Lorna Kapunan acknowledged outside the courtroom that Boransing’s testimony was not new but said it reaffirmed what had emerged during the House inquiry.
“The truth being the testimony in the House showed that the confidential funds were not used for this, and that was just affirmed,” Kapunan said.
She said the House proceedings were an inquiry in aid of legislation, not a trial, making the Senate impeachment court the proper venue for the evidence.
Intelligence for safety

Boransing also clarified the role of military intelligence in the programs after Senator-judge Sherwin Gatchalian asked whether the Army used intelligence information in choosing locations for the YLS and IEC.
Yes, but primarily to protect participants, Boransing said.
“The primary criteria is the safety of the students, the youth. So, the venue, wherever it is, has to be safe from attacks and other things,” he said.
DepEd provided open-source information about students, including potential youth leaders and schools that could host the activities.
Intelligence gathering and processing, however, were handled by AFP intelligence units, not civil-military operations personnel, Boransing said.
The distinction figured in questions about whether the activities could justify confidential- or intelligence-fund spending.
Boransing maintained that his certification did not attest to any such spending.
Senator-judge Joel Villanueva asked what he intended when he issued certifications for the joint YLS and school campaigns.
Boransing said he was merely certifying that the routine civil-military activities had been conducted and that participating agencies were present.

Asked why his unit did not question DepEd’s request despite having no role in its confidential-fund use, Boransing said: “For me personally sir, I had no reaction sir. We were preoccupied with very important security matters in our area of operation.”
‘No’ Duterte attendance
Senator-judge Raffy Tulfo asked whether Duterte attended any of the Army’s YLS activities in 2023.
Boransing said, “No.”
Boransing and Panopio were the eighth and ninth prosecution witnesses, respectively, for Article I, which deals with the alleged misuse of confidential funds.

The prosecution has previously presented Landbank officials who testified on the withdrawal of confidential funds by the OVP and DepEd, Commission on Audit auditors who examined the expenditures, and former OVP special disbursing officer Gina Acosta.
Acosta testified on Aug. 24 that she released P125 million in OVP confidential funds to then VPSPG chief Col. Raymund Dante Lachica in December 2022, despite knowing that he was not a bonded officer.
Like Boransing, Acosta had previously appeared before the House inquiry and said Duterte ordered the release of the funds to Lachica. /cb

articles.title: Dozens arrested after fatal pre-dawn shootout in Dutch village
articles.summary:
Police urged people in Overasselt to stay indoors after one person died and 34 were arrested

Authorities have arrested 34 people, including French, Belgian and Algerian nationals, after a…

blocks.text: Authorities have arrested 34 people, including French, Belgian and Algerian nationals, after a person died in a pre-dawn shootout in a Dutch village reportedly linked to a notorious drug lord.
Police urged people in Overasselt, near the German border, to stay indoors with doors and windows shut in case further suspects were on the loose.
At about 4am on Tuesday, a group of heavily armed men in balaclavas approached a house in Overasselt and shots were fired, resulting in the death of a 51-year-old, reportedly a security guard.

Police responding to the scene immediately came under fire, with two officers sustaining non-life-threatening injuries, police spokesperson Jolanda Aalbers said. Several weapons, data storage devices and vehicles were also seized, she said.
According to local media, the shootout was likely connected to the criminal underworld of Dutch drug lord Jos Leijdekkers, also known as Bolle Jos (fat Jos).
Leijdekkers is one of the Netherlands’ most wanted criminals and has previously been convicted for his role in international cocaine trafficking.

blocks.caption: From left: Monique Vinkesteijn, Joerie Minses and Jolanda Aalbers at a press conference following the shooting. Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock

blocks.text: He has lived in Sierra Leone for at least three years and is reportedly in a relationship with the daughter of the country’s president, Julius Maada Bio.
The Het Parool newspaper said the gunfight resulted from a conflict over several hundred kilograms of cocaine thought to have been trafficked by Leijdekkers’ gang.
Deputy chief prosecutor Monique Vinkesteijn said there had been a shooting at the same house last year related to a “longstanding conflict” but did not reveal further details.
“We know that the group currently in custody is international in nature,” Vinkesteijn said. “It includes French and Belgian nationals, people from Algeria, and also individuals from the Netherlands.”
after newsletter promotion
The prosecutor said the suspects faced a variety of charges ranging from murder to manslaughter to preparing a kidnapping and that it was possible further arrests would follow.
Local mayor Joerie Minses said the whole community was shocked by the violent events.
“What happened in Overasselt crosses all boundaries. This is un-Dutch … Overasselt has been shocked by a form of extreme violence that is totally unacceptable,” he said.

articles.title: Ariana Grande ends tour and steps back from public life
articles.summary: The star makes an emotional farewell as she wraps up a tour she's described as her "last hurrah".

blocks.text: Ariana Grande made an emotional exit on Tuesday night, as she wrapped up her Eternal Sunshine tour, and prepared to step back from public life.
The singer was occasionally close to tears - most notably during One Last Time, the song that took on extra meaning as an anthem for survivors of the 2017 Manchester terror attack.
"London, I'm going to need you to help me on this one," she said, kneeling down to be near the audience throughout the performance.
Last month, Grande announced a break from all future public-facing appearances following months of intense speculation about her health and appearance.
The step-back includes Grande's withdrawal from a production of Stephen Sondheim's Sunday in the Park with George at London's Barbican next summer.
She was due to appear alongside her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey. He also pulled out of the production on Tuesday.
On stage in London, Grande showed no signs of fragility or poor health - other than a foot injury that required her to swap her trademark stilettos for a succession of knee-high platform boots.
Nonetheless, she sprang across the stage in sync with her dancers, often on tip-toe to compensate for the lost height of her high heels.
But her composure slipped during the song Nowhere, Nobody, as she sang the line: "Hard to believe in a perfect ending."
The blip was short-lived, though. Professional to the core, Grande was never less than magnetic on stage.

Even before that announcement, Grande had described the Eternal Sunshine tour - which started in the US in June - as "one last hurrah", saying she wanted to take more acting roles after her Oscar-nominated performance in Wicked.
That meant her 10 show residency at London's O2 Arena represented many fans' last chance to see her in concert.
They flew in from all over the world - from China and Australia and cities all across Europe - with 200,000 people attending the London dates alone.
On the second night, Grande surprised the audience by bringing out her Wicked co-star Cynthia Erivo for a rendition of their movie duet For Good.
Across the board, reviews were positive.

"There's no question about it - Ariana Grande is one of the best singers of her generation," wrote Rolling Stone magazine, external, noting that "there were no signs" of the singer "struggling or not wanting to be there".
The Telegraph called the show "flawless", external, praising its "Hollywood-indebted" staging, and Grande's "genuine affection for Britain".
The BBC's review highlighted quieter songs like Imperfect For You, describing them as "delicate and gorgeous and strangely intimate in a room of 20,000 people".

But Guardian writer Kate Solomon said she was "gripped by genuine concern", external for Grande, even when she was enjoying the show, adding: "I really hope this tour does not go down in history for the wrong reasons".
The NME, by contrast, was left breathless by the star's physical prowess.
"Throughout the show," marvelled Nick Levine, external, "she skips across the stage in skyscraper heels that most drag performers would baulk at."
That wasn't the case on the final night, however, due to what Grande described as a "deep cut" on her foot.
Writing on Instagram, she assured fans the injury wasn't serious, insisting she was "on the mend" and would complete her final shows "even if I am a few inches shorter than usual".
She did so with a huge smile spread across her face, leaning into the big notes of Dangerous Woman, and sprinting across the stage during Break Free - one of many up-tempo highlights.
She ended the show as she always does - attached to a harness, ascending into the rafters of the O2 and disappearing.
Fans were left wondering when, if ever, they'd see her perform again.

articles.title: Relief as Australians missing in Nepal-Tibet flood disaster found alive
articles.summary: Five missing Australians have been found since Tuesday morning, bringing the total citizens unaccounted for to 38

blocks.text: A total of five Australians missing after devastating floods ravaged the Nepal-Tibet border last week have been found.
Of the five Australians confirmed safe, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet, one in China and three outside the crisis-hit area. The total number still missing is 38.
These Australians had not spoken to families and next of kin since the disaster struck seven days ago.
The department of foreign affairs and trade (Dfat) has received nearly 800 calls in relation to the floods, with 18 Australian personnel having travelled to Nepal to join staff on the ground.
More humanitarian and disaster relief from Australia is due to arrive in Nepal this afternoon.
Another Australian, 25-year-old Cara Severino, was safely located last week.
After an Australian made contact with family and Dfat yesterday, foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, said the government was “incredibly thankful”.
“It’s hard to imagine the sense of relief their loved ones must be feeling after what will have been an incredibly harrowing few days.”
The death toll from the ⁠unprecedented deluge of ice, rock, mud ​and debris on Wednesday last week has risen to 939 people, with 16 more dead reported in Tibet.
More than 4,400 people are missing.
Wong said the government needed to “remain realistic” about the days ahead.
“Communications remain difficult, infrastructure has been destroyed and many areas are still difficult to reach,” she said.
“As each day passes, our grave concerns for those still unaccounted for inevitably grow.”
“Our thoughts remain firmly with all those waiting for news of family and friends, and with the search and rescue teams working in extraordinarily difficult circumstances.”
Australia has sent a $8m assistance package for affected communities on the border between Nepal and the Chinese region of Tibet.
Nepal has deployed nearly 20,000 security personnel to support search and rescue, and Chinese state media has reported that 2,141 emergency personnel have been deployed.

articles.title: DOT eyes more visa-free gateways for Chinese tourists
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Spurred by a surge in Chinese tourist arrivals following relaxed visa rules, the Department of Tourism (DOT) is pushing to expand the 14-day visa-free scheme beyond the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Spurred by a surge in Chinese tourist arrivals following relaxed visa rules, the Department of Tourism (DOT) is pushing to expand the 14-day visa-free scheme beyond the country’s main gateways to draw more visitors to secondary destinations.

Tourism Secretary Dita Angara-Mathay said that aside from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (Naia) in Metro Manila and Mactan-Cebu International Airport in Cebu, the DOT wants the visa-free arrangement extended to other gateways serving major tourist destinations, including Clark, Caticlan, Palawan and Bohol, among others.

“If we’re going to get all the other agencies to sign up on this, then we can expect a lot more charter flights from China and a lot more arrivals,” Angara-Mathay said on the sidelines of the DOT’s partnership renewal with online booking platform Klook on Tuesday.

According to her, the DOT has prepared a position paper laying out the economic case for the expansion, backed by statistical analysis showing what she described as the “profound effect” of easier visa access on Philippine tourism.
Booming Chinese arrivals

Based on preliminary eTravel registrations, China recorded the biggest jump in tourist arrivals from January to August, with 310,088 visitors so far this year, up 69.15 percent year-on-year—an increase that the DOT chief said strengthens the case for expanding the visa-free arrangement.
“Can you imagine if you expand to cover more areas?” Angara-Mathay said.
That made China the country’s fourth-largest source of foreign visitors behind the United States, South Korea and Japan.

Overall, the Philippines recorded about 4.11 million arrivals as of Aug. 31 based on eTravel data. The DOT is targeting between 6.4 million and 6.8 million arrivals this year, although Angara-Mathay said reaching 7 million remains possible.
“It looks like, and we might just be sure to hit this target. And even more, especially if we’re able to get more tourist arrivals from target markets,” she said.
Secondary cities push
Apart from expanding visa-free entry, the DOT is pushing for more air links between secondary cities in the Philippines and key overseas markets, according to Tourism Assistant Secretary Ren Sapitan.
Tourism Undersecretary Stanley Ng, a former Philippine Airlines president, has been leading talks with carriers on potential new services, particularly involving China and South Korea.

Rather than concentrating connectivity on major hubs such as Seoul, the DOT wants airlines to explore secondary cities abroad and link them through charter flights to Philippine destinations such as Bohol and Caticlan. /cb

articles.title: ‘Foreign malign influence’ going ‘street level’ – AFP
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — “Foreign malign influence (FMI)” operations targeting the Philippines are adopting a more “street-level” approach, using the Filipino language to integrate themselves into…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — “Foreign malign influence (FMI)” operations targeting the Philippines are adopting a more “street-level” approach, using the Filipino language to integrate themselves into divisive domestic issues and thus becoming harder to detect, a military official said on Tuesday.

Reservist Rear Adm. Roy Vincent Trinidad, the Armed Forces of the Philippines spokesperson on the West Philippine Sea (WPS), said the shift became apparent in the “first quarter” of the year, as the WPS maritime issue became linked to other local controversies.

The intended discourse “used to be clearly identifiable as pro-Davao [when it comes to] West Philippine Sea issues,” Trinidad said in a press briefing. But “today, the formalized influence approach is they meddle with local issues.”

He cited the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, the flood control scandal, and criticism against President Marcos and Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr. among the issues the AFP is monitoring for possible FMIs.
Raid on Chinese-run firm
One local issue which, he said, has been exploited by foreign propaganda is the May 15 raid on Chinese-run Philippine Sanjia Steel Corp.

The raid at an ecozone in Misamis Oriental led to the arrest of 69 Chinese nationals and the discovery of radioactive materials in the Sanjia plant. The Chinese Embassy at the time filed a diplomatic protest over the arrests.
Trinidad said “It is now more difficult to detect [foreign influence] because it is already mixing with local issues.”
He also said the language “now is [more] prevalent in Tagalog,” whereas “before, it was mostly in English.”
“Attacks on the SND (secretary of national defense), attacks on [Rear Adm.] Jay Tarriela are now in Tagalog,” Trinidad noted. Tarriela serves as Philippine Coast Guard spokesperson on WPS issues.
He also noted a shift in language among officials of the Chinese Embassy.
“When it’s the deputy spokesperson of the Chinese Embassy, they use Tagalog and street-level [phrasing]. When it’s the spokesman of the Chinese Embassy, his tone is diplomatic,” Trinidad said.
This shift to a more informal messaging may be part of efforts to make social-media content harder to identify as foreign and more acceptable to Filipinos, Trinidad said.
“Definitely, this is part of their approach. They are adjusting to make it more acceptable to our fellow countrymen, so they can conceal it better,” he said.
In an advice to netizens encountering such content, he said: “Before ‘liking,’ before forwarding, before clicking, make sure carefully if what you are reading is true.” /cb

articles.title: Budget watchdog flags ‘worrying’ House tradition on OP budget
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The decision of House lawmakers not to subject to scrutiny the proposed 2027 budget of the Office of the President (OP) may have violated the checks and balances enshrined in…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The decision of House lawmakers not to subject to scrutiny the proposed 2027 budget of the Office of the President (OP) may have violated the checks and balances enshrined in the 1987 Constitution, according to a budget watchdog.

On Tuesday, the House appropriations committee voted 37-5 to swiftly end debate on the P10.1-billion proposed budget of the OP, citing parliamentary courtesy. The 2027 budget is 63.9-percent lower than this year’s P28.1 billion.

“The traditional practice of ‘courtesy’ to executive agencies afforded to the President … violates the checks and balances designed by the Constitution,” Kenneth Abante, coconvener of watchdog People’s Budget Coalition, told the Inquirer in a text message.
He described the practice as “worrying.”

“There are also red flags in the Office of the President’s budget that need to be scrutinized. At the very least, it should be debated so it can be discussed,” Abante said. “After all, it is still the people’s money being used, and it deserves the same scrutiny.”

Some programs flagged by budget watchdogs include confidential and intelligence funds allotted to the OP and funding for the government’s anticommunist task force, alongside its direct oversight authority over a support fund for local units, according to Tim Salomon of the Caucus of Development Non-Government Organizations Network.
Lawmakers have traditionally refrained from scrutinizing the OP’s budget, invoking the long-standing parliamentary courtesy extended to a sitting President.
Opposition lawmakers, however, protested the House appropriation committee’s move.

“Public funds are not personally owned by Malacañang and we do not want to continue the broken tradition of extending parliamentary courtesy [to] the Office of the President,” Kabataan Rep. Renee Co told lawmakers in a manifestation after she voted against terminating the OP’s budget hearing.
“The power of the purse is held by the legislature … and it should not be surrendered to the executive,” Co said.
Secret funds

Deputy Minority Leader and ACT Teachers Rep. Antonio Tinio also questioned why half of the President’s proposed budget next year falls under secret funds, stressing that transparency should be applied across all agencies.
Of the P10.1 billion, around P4.56 billion is earmarked for spending beyond traditional scrutiny.

Confidential and intelligence funds finance surveillance and intelligence information gathering activities, according to a 2015 joint circular between the Commission on Audit (COA) and several agencies.
Tinio said the OP should explain its allotments meant for secret expenses, especially amid the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, who is accused of misusing confidential funds.

“If [Duterte’s] P612.5 million in confidential funds is under scrutiny … why is the Office of the President not explaining why its confidential and intelligence funds are that big?” he asked, adding: “We need a fair application of the principle of transparency.”
Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, however, said that President Marcos has the right to hold secret funds as the nation’s chief executive.
He also noted that the COA had rendered an unmodified opinion on OP finances, which he described as “the highest opinion ever for all government agencies.”

“The President is the chief executive officer. The President is the head of state, so his first job is to ensure law and order and that is where confidential funds are being used,” Recto told reporters. /cb

articles.title: DOH: Better mask up amid haze from Indonesia forest fires
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Transboundary haze from the forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, may persist in parts of the Philippines until Thursday as the prevailing southwest monsoon or “habagat” causes…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Transboundary haze from the forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, may persist in parts of the Philippines until Thursday as the prevailing southwest monsoon or “habagat” causes smoke to reach several regions in Luzon and the Visayas, environment and health officials said on Tuesday.

Several cities in Metro Manila also recorded “very unhealthy” to “acutely unhealthy” air quality levels on Tuesday morning, according to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources’ Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB).

The Department of Health (DOH) advised the public to try staying indoors or wear an N95 mask when outdoors due to poor air quality attributed to haze. Those without an N95 mask may also use a wet handkerchief or cloth to cover their mouths and noses, or use two surgical or ordinary masks.
The DOH said haze can cause difficulty in breathing, coughing, chest pain, watering of the eyes, itchiness in the nose, and could worsen respiratory diseases, such as asthma.
“Extra caution is essential for children, the elderly, and those with respiratory and heart illnesses,” the DOH said.
Those without an N95 mask may also use a wet handkerchief or cloth, or two surgical or normal masks worn to form double layers.
‘Beyond our control’
According to Jundy del Socorro, chief of the Environmental Quality Management Division of DENR-EMB, haze may continue to affect parts of the country until Thursday.

“At this point, the haze situation is largely beyond our control because it depends on several factors outside the Philippines, including the intensity of the forest fires in Kalimantan, prevailing wind patterns, and rainfall across the region,” Del Socorro said.
Rainfall, he said, can help lower pollution levels by removing smoke particles and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) from the atmosphere.
PM2.5 refers to fine particles measuring 2.5 micrometers or smaller that can be inhaled deep into the lungs. Elevated levels can pose greater risks to people sensitive to air pollution.
“Between Sept. 4 and Sept. 6, air quality could gradually improve if rainfall remains widespread and wind patterns begin to shift,” said Del Socorro.

“Beyond Sept. 6, conditions will depend primarily on whether the fires in Kalimantan continue to generate smoke, whether new hot spots emerge, and whether winds continue to carry smoke toward the Philippines,” he added.
‘Acutely unhealthy’ areas

Data from the DENR-EMB as of 4 p.m. Tuesday showed the following areas in Metro Manila with “acutely unhealthy” levels of air quality: Parañaque (air quality index of 265), Las Piñas (245), Quezon City (237, Ateneo area), Malabon (227), Taguig (226), Manila (225), Valenzuela (221), Marikina (217), Muntinlupa (216), San Juan (214), and Mandaluyong (208).
Under the EMB scale, “acutely unhealthy” with an air quality index ranging from 201-300 is the second highest category, next to “emergency” with an air quality index of 301-500.
Areas under the “very unhealthy” category include Makati (188), Navotas (180), Quezon City (171, Commonwealth), and Pateros (167).

In a separate Facebook post, the DENR-EMB said among the regions affected by the haze included Central Luzon, Calabarzon (Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Rizal, Quezon) and Mimaropa (Mindoro, Marinduque, Romblon, Palawan).

Bernardo Rafaelito Alejandro IV, Office of Civil Defense deputy administrator for administration, reminded motorists to use headlights or fog lights when traveling at night or in areas with poor visibility.
Visayas situation
In Bohol, residents in Tagbilaran City and nearby towns reported hazy, smoke-filled skies, with some saying the condition had been observed since Monday.
Mel Micayabas, 34, of Dauis town, said Panglao Island appeared to be covered in smoke when viewed from a distance.
From Tagbilaran, neighboring Cebu Island, which is usually visible across the Bohol Strait, was barely seen through the thick haze. The mountains of Maribojoc were likewise obscured.
Air quality in Metro Cebu reached the “very unhealthy” level on Tuesday morning, according to the DENR-EMB in Central Visayas.
Bohol Gov. Erico Aristotle Aumentado urged residents to wear masks when going outdoors and avoid unnecessary exposure to the haze.
In Western Visayas, residents of Tubungan town in Iloilo also reported hazy conditions on Monday, with some saying the air smelled strongly of smoke and caused discomfort as they breathe.

Despite the haze, Iloilo City’s air quality remained within the “Good to Fair” range from Aug. 28 to 31, according to the latest monitoring results. —WITH REPORTS FROM GABRYELLE DUMALAG, HAZEL VILLA, AND LEO UDTOHAN

articles.title: Baguio’s Burnham Lake reopens after yearlong closure
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — Burnham Lake reopened to the public on Tuesday, coinciding with Baguio City’s 117th Charter Day celebration and bringing back boat rides at one of the city’s most iconic…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY, Philippines — Burnham Lake reopened to the public on Tuesday, coinciding with Baguio City’s 117th Charter Day celebration and bringing back boat rides at one of the city’s most iconic tourist attractions.
The man-made lake had been closed since October 2025 for a P480-million rehabilitation and improvement project.

Mayor Benjamin Magalong, Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (Tieza) General Manager and Chief Operating Officer Mark Lapid, Rep. Mauricio Domogan, Vice Mayor Faustino Olowan and other city officials led the ribbon-cutting ceremony.
The reopening came after the lake was enclosed by galvanized steel barriers as Tieza undertook extensive repairs and a makeover of the century-old attraction.
The rehabilitation formed part of the national government’s broader program to modernize Burnham Park and other tourism destinations in Baguio.

The 33-hectare park, including its nearly 4-hectare lake, was part of the original 1903 Burnham Plan prepared by American architect and urban planner Daniel Burnham. The park was designed as one of the city’s major open spaces and remains among Baguio’s most visited public attractions.
Baguio was established as a mountain resort city under the American colonial government and was formally granted a city charter on Sept. 1, 1909.

The rehabilitation of Burnham Park had been programmed as early as 2013 as part of a national tourism redevelopment initiative covering Baguio and Boracay. While the Boracay rehabilitation was completed in 2018, the Baguio project was delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic. A P500-million allocation originally intended for the city was instead used for pandemic response measures.
Improvements

The work included the construction of a wooden boardwalk around the roughly 10-meter-deep lake, concrete benches that also serve as reinforced embankments, and improvements to the view deck. About 14 new boats had also been brought to the lake grounds.
The lake normally holds about 34,000 cubic meters of water.
Returning concessionaires were previously asked to provide new boats instead of the swan-shaped boats that had long been associated with the attraction.
The Department of Tourism recorded 117,137 visitors arriving in Baguio from Dec. 15 to Dec. 31, 2025.
The city government, however, clarified that the reopening of Burnham Lake does not mean all areas of Burnham Park have reopened. Some facilities remain subject to safety assessments.

Tieza is also validating city plans for the next phase of the Burnham Park rehabilitation, which will cover Children’s Park, Skating Rink and Rose Garden, where a bust of Burnham stands. —MAUREEN MATAYEW

articles.title: Bodies of 2 SUV passengers found after Tarlac bridge collapse
articles.summary: TARLAC CITY, Philippines — The bodies of two of the four missing occupants of a sport utility vehicle (SUV) that plunged into the Tarlac River following the partial collapse of Agana Bridge on Aug.…

blocks.text: TARLAC CITY, Philippines — The bodies of two of the four missing occupants of a sport utility vehicle (SUV) that plunged into the Tarlac River following the partial collapse of Agana Bridge on Aug. 29 were recovered on Tuesday in separate areas of Pangasinan.

The remains of James Patrick Taborlupa were snagged in the net of a fishing vessel off Lingayen around 10 a.m. Hours later, the body of Shanen Tuhao was found in Bayambang, according to the Tarlac City government.
The lone survivor, 20-year-old Nataniel Dizon, said he had to save himself after the vehicle was swept away. —MADELLE CALAYAG AND YOLANDA SOTELO

articles.title: 11 mining protesters in Nueva Vizcaya released on bail
articles.summary: BAYOMBONG, NUEVA VIZCAYA, Philippines — The 11 residents of Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya, who were arrested by police on Aug. 28 on charges of grave coercion and resistance and disobedience, have been…

blocks.text: BAYOMBONG, NUEVA VIZCAYA, Philippines — The 11 residents of Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya, who were arrested by police on Aug. 28 on charges of grave coercion and resistance and disobedience, have been released after posting bail on Tuesday.
The 11 were among residents who had barricaded an area in Barangay Paquet to oppose the mining exploration activities of North Luzon Mineral Resources Corp. (NLMRC).
They were arrested when police moved to clear a blockade that allegedly sought to prevent the entry of fuel intended for the company’s exploration activities.
The protesters were ordered to post a total of P401,610 in bail, or P36,510 each.
Their release came as Bishop Jose Elmer Mangalinao of Bayombong called for a “fair” and “lawful” dialogue between the mining company and villagers opposing its exploration activities.
In a pastoral statement on Sunday, Mangalinao urged authorities to resolve the dispute through “due process” and asked police and the courts to “look beyond the charges” filed against the protesters.
“Let us not look only at the charges written on paper. Let us also see the people behind those charges,” Mangalinao said.

The bishop said the protesters’ poverty should not diminish their rights and questioned what he described as the “haphazard” arrests and mining activities conducted without adequate hearing or consultation.
“It does not mean that if they are poor, they have fewer rights,” Mangalinao said.
Permit

He also said villagers had the “right” to oppose the exploration because their health, safety and the environment—including their farms, water sources and forests—as well as their children’s future were at stake.
NLMRC obtained a permit in May 2025 for gold and copper exploration covering 4,456 hectares in Barangay Paquet.
The area is claimed by villagers to form part of the ancestral domain of Bugkalot and Ilongot indigenous communities.
Mangalinao, Fr. Christian Dumangeng, an antimining advocate, and other community members have also faced charges over their opposition to the exploration activities.

Their lawyer has raised the possibility that the cases could constitute a strategic lawsuit against public participation, or SLAPP, which he described as an effort to discourage villagers and advocacy groups from advocating environmental protection and community rights.
Tensions escalated on Aug. 28 when police moved to clear the blockade against fuel trucks, resulting in the arrest of the 11 protesters. Two other villagers were hospitalized during the incident.

Provincial and municipal officials, including Gov. Jose Gambito and Kasibu Vice Mayor Alberto Bumolo Jr., have since negotiated with the protesters for a temporary agreement to keep NLMRC personnel and equipment out of the site while talks continue. /cb

articles.title: DOF: VAT-free power fee may cost gov’t P10B
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The government could lose an estimated P10 billion annually from the planned removal of the 12-percent value-added tax (VAT) on electricity system loss charges, the Department…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The government could lose an estimated P10 billion annually from the planned removal of the 12-percent value-added tax (VAT) on electricity system loss charges, the Department of Finance (DOF) said.

Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of an event, Finance Secretary Frederick Go confirmed the estimated revenue loss, saying the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) is still awaiting the Energy Regulatory Commission’s (ERC) policy decision before processing the matter.
System losses refer to electricity that is generated but lost during transmission and distribution, with the cost recovered by power firms from consumers through the system loss charge.

In Resolution No. 26 published on Aug. 28, the ERC declared the system loss charge a government-mandated pass-through cost that would no longer form part of the gross sales of generation companies, the National Grid Corp. of the Philippines and distribution utilities. The resolution will take effect once the BIR issues the necessary confirmation.
Distribution utilities will then have 60 days to modify their billing formats to reflect that the system loss charge is not subject to VAT.

The policy comes over a month after President Marcos, in his State of the Nation Address, called for the removal of system loss charges in electricity bills to ease the financial burden of Filipinos. —NYAH GENELLE C. DE LEON

articles.title: Thieves steal $70,000 worth of beer
articles.summary: MONTCLAIR, California — Thieves made off with tens of thousands of cans of Pabst beer in two separate heists from a Southern California warehouse on the same day, police said. Pabst Blue Ribbon has…

blocks.text: MONTCLAIR, California — Thieves made off with tens of thousands of cans of Pabst beer in two separate heists from a Southern California warehouse on the same day, police said.

Pabst Blue Ribbon has turned the thefts—valued by police at $70,000—into a light-hearted social media promotion. But police in Montclair said on Friday that investigators are trying to determine whether they were part of a single operation.
In the first heist, about $45,000 worth of beer headed to Tucson, Arizona, was picked up but never delivered, according to police.

An hour later, a “purported subcontracting company” submitted fake documents to pick up another $25,000 worth of beer, Montclair police said in a news release. Both thefts occurred on Aug. 17 at an Anheuser-Busch distribution center about 65 kilometers east of Los Angeles.
Roughly 34,000 cans of Pabst Blue Ribbon and non-alcoholic Old Milwaukee beer—more than 1,500 cases—were stolen, according to a police report obtained by the Los Angeles Times.
In Instagram posts, Pabst put the weight of the stolen cargo at 18,145 kilograms and started a countdown seeking its return.

“To the thief: we don’t fault you for wanting to brag to your friends how much PBR you have, we just wish you obtained it the honorable way,” the company wrote. It added, “P.s. this is real and we are deadly serious.” /cb

Jordan's military says Iranian missiles intercepted
The Jordanian Armed Forces said that 10 ballistic missiles launched from Iran had been intercepted, while another three landed in remote areas.

"Jordan's air defence systems engaged 13 ballistic missiles that entered the Kingdom's airspace, successfully intercepting and destroying 10 of them, while three missiles fell in remote areas away from populated centres," a Jordanian military statement stated. blocks.text: Albanese announces $600m package to combat drug smuggling in Pacific
Australia will step up its support to fight trans-national drug trafficking flowing through the Pacific, with a $600m package.
Anthony Albanese announced the new investment at the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, which aims to stop the contraband arriving in Australia.
The increase in drug flow across the Pacific is a huge problem in several countries: linked to increased gang activity in Samoa and Tonga, and a sharp rise in the HIV rate in Fiji.
Heightened activity is showing up in Australian Federal Police interventions of narcotics in the region.
In 2025, about 4.6 tonnes of illicit drugs were seized by local and international law enforcement, the Australian Federal Police reported.
In the first five months of this year, 17 tonnes have been picked up - mostly cocaine.
The new package – which will be opt-in for Pacific countries – will include enhanced aerial surveillance, and police and border training.
“Drug trafficking is having a devastating impact on Pacific communities,” Pacific minister Pat Conroy said.
“This initiative responds to the calls of regional leaders to do more, and to step up regional coordination to address this scourge.”

blocks.text: Chanel Contos to call for social media opt-in algorithm

blocks.caption: Achol Arok

blocks.text: Achol Arok
Consent education advocate Chanel Contos will urge Australia to enforce a social media opt-in algorithm to help reduce the influence of the “manosphere” on both men and women.
Contos will deliver a speech about the harms of social media algorithms in Australia in an address to the National Press Club in Canberra at midday.
Contos is expected to say:

double quotation markThis is crucial, and the detail in any reform will determine its success – as will be the overall strength of the proposed Digital Duty of Care reforms that are needed in their own right. It is too easy for Big Tech to design schemes that appear as structural reform but actually suit them just fine.

blocks.caption: Chanel Contos will speak at the National Press Club in Canberra at midday today.  Photograph: Mick Tsikas/AAP

blocks.text: The Teach Us Consent CEO will point to examples of algorithmic harms such as the “manosphere”, accusing bad actors of jumping on to “a market opportunity” that has misogyny “at the heart of its business model”.

double quotation markIt usually starts with something as harmless as a workout video, or motivational content. Very quickly, boys and men are taken into the “manosphere”, communities that persistently promote the idea that emotional control, material wealth, and physical appearance and dominance, especially over women, are markers of male worth. This is harmful to the individual man consuming this content, and then anyone else close to him in life, including other men, but disproportionately women and girls.
Welcome
Good morning and welcome to our live news blog. I’m Martin Farrer with the top overnight stories and then it’ll be Nick Visser with the main action.

articles.title: Deported Milo Yiannopoulos says he is ‘ashamed’ of support for Trump
articles.summary:
British far-right pundit breaks silence on ICE arrest and deportation and says he was ‘really, really terrified’

Milo Yiannopoulos, the British far-right commentator who was

blocks.text: Milo Yiannopoulos, the British far-right commentator who was arrested last week by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers in Louisiana and deported to the United Kingdom, has broken his silence about the experience, saying that “for the first time I know what it feels like to be really, really terrified”.

Yiannopoulos on Tuesday appeared on Piers Morgan Uncensored, a YouTube show presented by Piers Morgan, the British broadcaster and media personality. Yiannopoulos, 41, described the experience in the US as “humiliating and disorientating”, “physically degrading” and “frightening”.
He also said that he was “ashamed” of his previous support for Donald Trump, who has pursued an agenda of mass deportation throughout his second presidency.

“I didn’t really understand the physical reality of how institutionalized the brutality is in America” he said, adding: “It’s like everybody that’s arrested is an MS-13 gang member, and it hurts a lot more than it looks like on television.”
His remarks came just days after he was deported from the US, after being arrested on Thursday by ICE officers at New Orleans airport.

In a statement last week, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the parent agency of ICE, said Yiannopoulos had “legally entered the country” in May 2019, but “chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws”.

Yiannopoulos was an early supporter of Trump before he first became US president in 2016. He is a former editor of Breitbart News and later worked to help the rapper Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, explore a presidential run in 2024.
The homeland security department said Yiannopoulos was issued a final order of removal by an immigration judge on 22 July “after failing to show up for his immigration hearing”.

In the Piers Morgan interview, Yiannopoulos disputed the government’s account and denied previously overstaying a visa, He said he is married to an American, and claimed he held a green card that he was “renewing on a two-year basis”.
The Guardian has contacted homeland security and the White House for comment on Yiannopoulos’s remarks.
Yiannopoulos also said that while he was detained, “no one would tell me anything” – a common complaint from people held in ICE custody.

“I don’t think I’ve ever been frightened like that before” he told Morgan. “I think maybe in the past I’ve been a little bit blasé when people talked about their trauma, a little bit cavalier when people talked about stuff kind of lingering with them, but I get it now … I wouldn’t wish it on anyone.”
Last year, in posts on social media, Yiannopoulos had been supportive of Trump’s crackdown on immigration.

In one post, he wrote: “There is one concrete thing we must insist on this administration delivering. It matters a lot more than debts measured in imaginary money. We have got to deport millions and millions and millions of people. Without that, nothing else matters.”

In another post, Yiannopoulos had said that California “needs ICE checkpoints at supermarket entrances, gas stations, strip malls, intersections and government buildings, with on the spot deportation for anyone who can’t prove they are in the US legally”.

During Tuesday’s interview, Yiannopoulos said of his past support for Trump: “If I had any clue that anything remotely like this was even possible, I would never have gotten involved in supporting Trump in the first place and I’m very ashamed that I did.”

articles.title: In search for senior Hamas operative, Israeli raid on Gaza City camp kills 3 children
articles.summary: Four people were killed in a Gaza City displacement camp Tuesday in a raid Israel's defence minister said was to locate a senior Hamas official.

image.caption: Medics say three children were among the four dead during the military raid, which injured others and is at least the fifth in a series of attacks on the enclave in recent weeks that's left many dead and injured. (AFP via Getty Images)

blocks.text: World·New
Four people were killed in a Gaza City displacement camp Tuesday in a raid Israel's defence minister said was to locate a senior Hamas official.
Hamas called the attack a 'serious crime' that constitutes a 'deliberate disregard for civilian lives'
Israel Katz said the official was arrested following the raid, and an Israeli security official identified the man as the head of Hamas's internal security service to Reuters.

Near the strike, people's tents and belongings were burnt and ripped to pieces — remnants of a car were visible, mangled and blackened. Medics say three children were among the four dead during the military raid, which injured others and is at least the fifth in a series of attacks on the enclave in recent weeks that's left many dead and injured.

"Have mercy on us. They're children," Abu Al Abd, a Palestinian living in the camp who had been getting water with his children at the time of the raid, told CBC freelance videographer Mohamed El Saife.
Last week, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu warned of "targeted strikes" because children were flying kites that landed in Israeli territory.
"What kind of life is this?" Al Abd said. He says he doesn't care about the targets, he only cares about the children.
'All the children were screaming'
In a statement posted to Telegram, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that Hamas had "recently advanced attacks" against their troops and Israeli civilians.
"The terrorist was struck in order to remove that threat," they wrote on Tuesday. They also noted that their troops would remain deployed in the area in order to "remove any threat."

"This is our policy: We do not wait for threats, but rather pursue Hamas terrorists, thwart them and destroy their terror infrastructure," Katz told reporters Tuesday while visiting the Netiv HaAsara community in Israel.

items: Israel opens criminal probes over killings of 6-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab, Gaza rescue workers
3-year-old boy among 2 Palestinians killed by Israeli strike, Gaza medics say

blocks.text: Faiza al-Bahtini said her nephew was among the children killed on Tuesday.
"They were scared, their bodies were shaking, all the children were screaming," she said. "We, the adults, can't handle it."
The 50-year-old said this wasn't the first time her family has been caught in the middle of the fighting and lost loved ones as a result.
Ceasefire nearly 1 year old
Al-Bahtini was displaced with her family from the north after an attack last year led to the death of her 14-year-old nephew.
"Our homes were ruined, our lives were ruined and we have to move from one place to another."

The Gaza Health Ministry notes that over 1,300 civilians have died since Oct. 11, when a U.S.-backed ceasefire took effect and halted the large-scale fighting that had devastated the enclave, but it has not ended Israeli strikes.

The military has said such operations are intended to prevent attacks by Hamas and other Palestinian militant groups. It says four Israeli soldiers have been killed in militant attacks since the ceasefire began.

In a statement posted to Telegram, Hamas called Tuesday's attack a "serious crime" that constitutes a "deliberate disregard for civilian lives." They also said this was an "extension of the brutal genocide" against Palestinians that has continued despite the ceasefire.

The statement continued, saying that the attack reflected a "policy of defiance and arrogance" on Netanyahu's part. Finally, they called on mediators and the international community to stop Israel's ongoing violations of the agreement.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Yasmine Hassan is a producer in CBC's Ottawa bureau. From there, she covers developments inside Gaza and the West Bank related to the Israel-Hamas war. If you have a story idea, send news tips in English or Arabic to yasmine.hassan@cbc.ca.
With files from Mohamed El Saife and Reuters
