articles.title: Solon warns: Emojis being used for online drug trade
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — A lawmaker has sounded the alarm about illegal drug dealers being able to reach young people through social media by using emojis as codes for the products being sold. In a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A lawmaker has sounded the alarm about illegal drug dealers being able to reach young people through social media by using emojis as codes for the products being sold.

In a statement on Tuesday, Las Piñas Rep. Mark Anthony Santos said that authorities have found evidence of drug-related activities online, particularly on messaging platforms, where buyers and sellers use certain emojis—particularly icons deemed by the United States Drug Enforcement Agency as signs for drugs like methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy, and marijuana.

A code cheat sheet sent by Santos’ office showed that some illegal drugs are represented by usual signs like mushrooms for mushrooms; trees, fire, clouds, and clover leaves for marijuana; cocaine with snow, diamonds, or a snowman; to the more uncommon ones, meth with a diamond emoji or a blue heart; and heroin with a brown heart.

“Technically, all social media platforms prohibit the sale of drugs, but teens know how to find a drug dealer on social media. Drug enforcement units have found evidence that drug activity is rampant across major platforms, particularly Messenger and Viber in the Philippines,” Santos said.

“Social media has made it possible for drug dealers to operate in plain sight. They can use coded words, images, emojis, and seemingly harmless posts to advertise illegal drugs while trying to evade the platforms’ detection systems,” he added.

According to the lawmaker, some social media sites have become a recruitment hub for online drug trafficking, as experienced users are supposedly able to locate dealers through seemingly ordinary posts and interactions.

Furthermore, Santos said that cybersecurity experts have also reported that popular online games and social media platforms are also being tapped as recruitment grounds for another purpose—to engage in nihilistic violent extremist (NVE) behavior or senseless violence.
NVE is being looked at as an angle in the recent shooting incidents in Tacloban City and Zamboanga.
Such activities, Santos said, only stress the need for social media restrictions.
“Criminals are adapting faster than we are. They are learning how to use the same platforms where our young people spend much of their time,” he noted.

Last August, Santos threw his support for proposals seeking to restrict social media use for children aged 14 and below, amid fears that the internet is being used by drug syndicates to recruit young people and even engage in drug trade.
Santos said he backs the proposal that would ban children from accessing social media—which was also supported by Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla.

Remulla, during the hearing of the House of Representatives’ committee on appropriations on the proposed 2027 budget of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), said that he agrees with the ban.
Just recently, the Senate committee on public information and mass media endorsed a bill seeking to set 16 years old as the minimum age for social media use.

Both moves came amid fears that unrestricted social media use may have led students behind the school shooting incidents at the San Jose National High School in Tacloban City last June 22 and the Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City last August 18 to do these actions.
Three students were killed during the Tacloban shooting, while two, including the gunman, were confirmed dead after the incident at Ateneo de Zamboanga University.
There is a belief that the perpetrators in both incidents were supposedly exposed to violent content online.

But Santos said that aside from violent content, the Philippines and other countries have faced problems regarding young children being recruited toward scrupulous activities, including drug trade. /cb

articles.title: Chinese national nabbed over alleged rogue cell site, phishing scheme
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has arrested a male Chinese national in General Trias, Cavite, for allegedly operating a rogue cellular site supposedly being used to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has arrested a male Chinese national in General Trias, Cavite, for allegedly operating a rogue cellular site supposedly being used to transmit fraudulent text messages and direct mobile users to a fake banking website.

NBI director Melvin Matibag said Tuesday that the bureau’s Special Action Unit (SAU) conducted an operation following an intelligence report it received on foreign nationals allegedly operating an International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) catcher in parts of southern Metro Manila.
The IMSI catcher can supposedly mimic legitimate cellular towers and interact with nearby mobile phones.
It was allegedly mounted inside a vehicle and moved through densely populated areas.
“Ang may possession nito ay isang foreign national, isang foreigner na umiikot, nakasakay sa sasakyan na ginagamit ito dun sa phishing, sa mga scams,” Matibag explained in an ambush interview.
(We tracked it down and confiscated it from a foreign national. This foreigner was driving around in a vehicle, using the device for phishing and scams.)
The messages deceitfully claimed it came from a legitimate source and directed recipients to a website designed to resemble that of a prominent Philippine bank.

“Kumokopya na parang signal siya ng tower kung saan pumapasok yung mga cellphone, yung signal ng cellphone, na maaaring gamitin ito para kuning mga information, kunin yung data ng credit card ninyo, na ginagamit ito pang scam,” Matibag noted.
(It mimics a cell tower signal that cell phones connect to, which can be used to gather information and steal your credit card data for scamming purposes.)
The agents arrested the suspect inside his residence after conducting physical surveillance and technical monitoring.
A separate rogue cellular site was also found at the location, the NBI said.
The suspect is facing violations of the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, as well as the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act.

The NBI emphasized that the case goes beyond financial fraud, noting that the unauthorized use of telecommunications equipment could pose a national security concern by allowing criminal groups to exploit communications infrastructure and reach large numbers of mobile users. — RENDELL IVAN MANUEL, INQUIRER.NET TRAINEE

articles.title: Pistol in a lake gives hope for French cold case
articles.summary: Saad al-Hilli was shot dead with his wife and mother-in-law while holidaying in eastern France in September 2012.

blocks.text: Police investigating the unsolved murder of a British family in France 14 years ago have an unexpected new clue with the discovery of a Luger pistol in the waters of a nearby lake.

One of the few certainties in the killings of Saad al-Hilli with his wife and mother-in-law – as well as a passing cyclist – is that they were shot through the head with a Luger model P06, a type used by the Swiss army until around 1960.
Now France's cold case unit has confirmed the discovery of a Luger in Lake Annecy, not far from the scene of the murders in September 2012.
According to Marianne magazine, which broke the story, it was British tourists on 20 August who found the weapon lying in two metres of water.
At first they thought it was a water pistol, but realised their mistake when they felt its weight.
The discovery was made near the very camping site – Le Solitaire du Lac – where the al-Hillis were staying in their caravan, Marianne reported.
Forensic experts are now examining the weapon, which has been badly damaged by its time under water, to see if it is indeed a P06 model.
It is estimated that around 60,000 Luger P06s were manufactured. But the number of Luger pistols in general that were made is more like three million.

Exhaustive investigations in France and the UK have left police no closer to understanding who carried out the al-Hilli murders and why. Over the years a series of leads have been pursued then dropped.
A British national of Iraqi birth, Saad al-Hilli was holidaying with his family in the picturesque countryside of Lake Annecy in eastern France.

On the afternoon of 5 September, his body with those of his wife and mother-in-law were found in their car, its motor still running, on a forest road near the village of Chevaline. A passing cyclist had – like the other victims – been shot through the head.

Poignantly, the two al-Hilli daughters, aged four and seven, survived. The older girl had been hit on the head with a pistol butt and was badly hurt. The younger, lying in the car under her mother's skirts, was not discovered till forensic experts began examining the scene many hours later.

It was fragments from the pistol butt which enabled police to identify it as a Luger P06. The model is regarded more as a collector's item than a working weapon, which made the theory of a professional hit against the family seem less likely.

Lake Annecy is only 50km from Switzerland, where the Luger P06 will have been familiar to older people from their military service. French police said many examples of the gun have been kept by families on either side of the border.
Among the theories that have been entertained are that the murders were linked to a family row over money; that they were the work of a motiveless crank; and that the main target was the cyclist.
Police were also briefly intrigued by the fact that al-Hilli's wife's first husband – an American – died of a heart attack just hours before the killings in France.

articles.title: SC: Affidavit of desistance cannot be used to dismiss trafficking case
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court (SC) has ruled that an affidavit of desistance, or a sworn statement withdrawing a complaint, from a victim of exploitation is considered “highly suspect” and…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Supreme Court (SC) has ruled that an affidavit of desistance, or a sworn statement withdrawing a complaint, from a victim of exploitation is considered “highly suspect” and cannot be used as a basis to dismiss a trafficking case.

In a decision promulgated on February 19, 2026, and made public on Tuesday, the high court’s Third Division affirmed the conviction of a woman involved in a qualified trafficking in persons involving a minor.
According to the SC, the woman recruited the minor, who was her neighbor, to provide sexual services to a man in exchange for money.
The minor received P15,000 from the man, but the recruiter later took the money, giving the victim only P3,000 and buying her a cellphone.
When the minor’s mother discovered the exploitation, she filed a complaint against the woman.
The victim testified before the court but later signed an affidavit of desistance to withdraw the charges.
Meanwhile, the minor admitted during the cross-examination that she only signed the affidavit of desistance prepared by the woman’s counsel because she was paid P30,000.
The Regional Trial Court convicted the woman of qualified trafficking in persons under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, as amended by the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012.
The Court of Appeals affirmed the decision, and the SC sustained the recruiter’s conviction.
The woman was sentenced to life imprisonment, fined P2 million, and ordered to pay the victim P600,000 in damages.
According to the SC, human trafficking cases must not be dismissed based on the affidavits of desistance executed by the victims, their parents, or legal guardians.
It pointed out that once a criminal case has been filed in court, the complainant can no longer decide if it will proceed.
The High Court emphasized that affidavits of desistance by victims of exploitation “should be treated with caution, as they may have been made under coercion, pressure, or undue influence.” /cb
“This is especially true when the victims are children, who may not fully understand the consequences of withdrawing their testimony,” said the SC.

articles.title: Iloilo City air quality worsens as Indonesia haze reaches Visayas
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY, Philippines — Air quality in parts of Iloilo City has deteriorated as transboundary haze from forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, spreads across portions of the Philippines, prompting…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY, Philippines — Air quality in parts of Iloilo City has deteriorated as transboundary haze from forest fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, spreads across portions of the Philippines, prompting local authorities to advise vulnerable residents to avoid outdoor physical activities.

The Iloilo City Operations Center (OpCen), in an advisory issued at 5 p.m. Tuesday, Sept. 1, said the haze was affecting portions of Luzon and the Visayas, with the prevailing southwest monsoon or “habagat” carrying particulate matter northward from Indonesia.

The advisory preceded a separate health warning released at 9 p.m. saying the haze had reached Western Visayas and could cause coughing, throat irritation, chest discomfort, and watery eyes, with people suffering from asthma and cardiovascular disease facing greater risks.
In Iloilo City, monitoring showed a marked increase in fine particulate pollution.
At the Environmental Management Bureau Region VI’s Garden of Love monitoring station, the PM2.5 Air Quality Index rose from readings classified as “Good” late last week to “Fair” on Aug. 31.
The station recorded AQI readings of 19 on Aug. 28, 34 on Aug. 29 and 41 on Aug. 30 before climbing to 70 on Aug. 31.

More concerning conditions were detected at the Central Philippine University/Ungka monitoring station, where real-time measurements cited by OpCen showed a US AQI of 116, classified as “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups,” with a PM2.5 concentration of 41.4 micrograms per cubic meter.

Regional satellite and PurpleAir monitoring also indicated elevated particulate levels over parts of Indonesia and scattered elevated concentrations along western and central Philippine corridors, according to the advisory.
OpCen said atmospheric analysis at an altitude of about three kilometers showed sustained southwesterly airflow transporting particulate matter from Indonesia across Philippine airspace.

An observable haze layer was documented Tuesday morning at moderate levels along affected corridors. Authorities warned that lighter surface and low-level winds in the afternoon could reduce the dispersal of pollutants, allowing fine particles to remain closer to the ground.
PM2.5 refers to microscopic airborne particles measuring 2.5 micrometers or smaller. Because of their size, the particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and may enter the bloodstream.

Exposure may trigger coughing, difficulty breathing, throat irritation, chest discomfort and watery eyes and can aggravate asthma, chronic bronchitis, heart disease and other existing respiratory or cardiovascular conditions, OpCen said.

Children, senior citizens, pregnant women and people with pre-existing respiratory or cardiovascular illnesses were advised to avoid outdoor physical activities and, as much as possible, remain indoors in areas with filtered air.

If going outdoors cannot be avoided, authorities strongly urged residents, particularly vulnerable individuals, to use properly fitted N95 masks or appropriate masks capable of filtering fine particulate matter.

Residents were also advised to keep doors and windows closed during periods when haze is at its worst, avoid low-lying areas where smoke and suspended particles may accumulate, and use air purifiers equipped with HEPA filters when available.
Motorists were told to exercise additional caution because haze may reduce visibility and to ensure that vehicle headlights or fog lights are working properly.
Those who experience difficulty breathing, persistent coughing, or chest pain were advised to seek medical attention immediately.

The Iloilo City Operations Center said it was continuing to monitor the haze and the southwest monsoon, together with information from the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration, its Visayas regional weather office, and other air-quality monitoring sources.
Authorities said further advisories could be issued depending on changes in atmospheric and air-quality conditions. /cb

articles.title: Germany terminates lease for Berlin's Russian House
articles.summary: Germany has announced the termination of the lease for the Russian House in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it is a hub for propaganda and espionage.

image.caption: The Russian House has been a fixture on Berlin's Friedrichstrasse since 1984Image: Schoening/picture alliance

blocks.text: Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has announced that the contract under which the Russian House is operated will be rescinded. This is one of several measures in retaliation for Russian involvement in the attempted airport drone attack at the Leipzig/Halle Airport on August 4.

The Russian House is centrally located on Friedrichstrasse in the heart of the German capital. As a throwback to a bygone era of friendly German-Russian relations, it has long been the subject of fierce disagreements and a bone of contention in Berlin.

The massive seven-story building covering an area of almost 30,000 square meters opened in 1984. At that time, back in the days of the East German state, its role was to celebrate friendship with the Soviet Union through concerts, film screenings and book readings. It even had its own small bookstore.
Leipzig drone threat prompts security concerns in Germany
French authorities have previously linked the building to possible activities by Russian intelligence services.

"In light of the measures taken against German cultural institutions and organizations, the federal government is comprehensively and continuously reviewing the legal basis of the Russian House under international treaty law,” said German Foreign Ministry spokesperson Martin Giese at a press conference in Berlin at the beginning of August.

Back then, in response to a question from DW about the organization's future activities, Giese emphasized that the fate of the Russian House is linked to that of the Goethe Institut in Moscow, and that any action taken against one would also have direct consequences for the other.
German tax money for Russian propaganda?

The property on Friedrichstrasse belongs to Germany, yet the building is run by the Russian agency Rossotrudnichestvo, the Federal Agency for the Commonwealth of Independent States, Compatriots Living Abroad and International Humanitarian Cooperation.

Rossotrudnichestvo, whose primary purpose is to promote the Russian language abroad, currently has dozens of similar institutions worldwide. The German Foreign Office has repeatedly stated that the employees of the institute have diplomatic status in Germany.

Since 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the agency has been on the EU sanctions list. At the time, the EU justified this by stating that the agency's goal was to consolidate "a wider public perception of the occupied Ukrainian territories as Russian."

blocks.caption: Symbols of friendship remained on display in Berlin's Russian House in October 2023, more than year after the Russian invasion of UkraineImage: Dmyrto Katkov/DW

blocks.text: Moscow still maintains that the Russian House is a place to celebrate the friendship between the two countries: "The Russian House is Russia's cultural embassy in the heart of Berlin," according to the Russian Embassy's website.
The events that take place there attract 200,000 visitors a year, according to Russian House organizers. Critics label them as propaganda.
Berlin media outlets have repeatedly reported on events at the in-house cinema where, for example, films were shown in which Ukrainian citizens were portrayed as Nazis.
Germany fears closure of Goethe-Institut in Moscow

The Russian House is owned by the Russian Federation, but the Federal Republic of Germany pays the property tax for the building on the basis of its legal obligation under the bilateral German-Russian agreement on property issues relating to cultural institutes.

Moscow and Berlin are also bound by the Intergovernmental Agreement on Cultural Cooperation, which was signed in December 1992 and entered into force in May 1993. It has a term of five years and is automatically extended for the same period unless one of the parties notifies the other at least six months before the expiration of the respective term.

Both agreements — regarding the property of the Russian House and the Goethe-Institut, as well as the cultural cooperation between Russia and Germany — remain in force even in the fifth year of Russia's war against Ukraine.

It is an open secret that the German government has been shying away from conflict over the Russian House because it fears the Russian government could respond by closing the Goethe-Institut in Moscow.
The institute was already forced to significantly scale back its operations in Russia in May 2023, when restrictions were imposed on the number of German officials in Russia.

A few weeks earlier, the Goethe-Institut's bank accounts in Russia were frozen in retaliation after the Berlin Public Prosecutor's Office opened a preliminary investigation against the Russian House for violating sanctions and ordered the freeze of its accounts.

So far, the Goethe-Institut continues to offer digital language courses in Russia. The libraries at its branches in Moscow and St. Petersburg continue to receive the latest German literature despite logistical difficulties, as representatives of the institute assured DW earlier this year.
Direct Russian-German contacts have become virtually impossible
In recent years, several German foundations in Russia have been classified as "undesirable organizations."
This includes the foundations run by Germany's established political parties.
Anyone who cooperates with "undesirable organizations" faces criminal prosecution in Russia. This makes all direct contact provided for in the cultural agreement virtually impossible.
This article was originally written in German and first published in August 2025. It was updated and republished in September 2026 to reflect news developments.

articles.title: River water smashed into tunnel and chased me for 20 minutes, Nepal worker tells BBC
articles.summary: Major efforts to rescue hydropower workers continue as Nepal's death toll exceeds 1,000.

blocks.text: River water smashed into tunnel and chased me for 20 minutes, Nepal worker tells BBC
Pemba Dundu Tamang tells the BBC how he discovered some of his colleagues were missing after he escaped a flooded tunnel
ByAshok Dahal and Kamal Pariyar
BBC NepaliReporting fromNuwakot, central Nepal
Nepalese hydropower workers have told the BBC about the catastrophic moment water from the Trishuli River crashed into their tunnel as the region was inundated by deadly flash floods last week.
It started with a sudden, strong gust of air, says Pemba Dundu Tamang, whose team of about 30 was constructing the tunnel's concrete lining.
The blast of wind sent plywood flying through the air and dislodged heavy machinery. Just outside, houses had already been swept away.
"I ran towards the tunnel entrance," he said. "The water was chasing behind me and I was running ahead of it."
Tamang lost several family members who were at home at the time. Nepal's death toll has exceeded 1,000 after last week's devastating floods, and officials say about 4,000 are missing.

A number of the missing - potentially in the hundreds - are labourers like Tamang, working in a vast network of tunnels at hydropower sites along the river. Engineers have been pumping air into these tunnels as part of a huge rescue operation.
"We are focused on search-and-rescue efforts at the tunnels, our work is continuing," Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP news agency.
"Our soldiers are also deployed to collect bodies and prevent the spread of disease."

blocks.caption: A BBC diagram illustrating (1) workers trapped in tunnels after the flooding (2) oxygen being pumped into the tunnels to help them breathe and (3) rescuers using a bulldozer to clear mud and rebris

blocks.text: Tamang says he ran for about 20 minutes to flee the violent deluge, which followed him uphill.
"I was almost unconscious with shock. I could not think clearly."
His colleague, Itha Ghale, says the powerful gust of air almost blew them away as they sprinted.
Over 99% of the electricity generated in Nepal comes from hydropower, and Tamang and Ghale had been working at a major production site helping to build the Upper Trishuli 3B Hydropower Project.
The plant, which was due to open next year, was designed to re-use water from a hydroelectric plant further upstream to generate additional electricity for Nepal's national grid.
There were several different teams operating there - and Tamang says the one operating the large tunnel-lining machine was the last to come out.
But soon afterwards came a crushing realisation.
"I could see where my house should have been. There was nothing left. That was when I realised everything was gone."
Six of Tamang's relatives - his mother, elder brother and sister-in-law and three of their children - are gone, he said. They were at home on the riverside when the floods hit.
Only his wife, son and one nephew survived.

blocks.caption: A map showing the location of the glacier collapse and hydropower plants along the Trishuli RIver

blocks.text: "I feel life is meaningless now. Surviving feels miserable. I do not know where to eat or where to go," Tamang says.
"The dead are at peace. It is those of us who survived who suffer."
Ghale, who lost eight members of his family, says he does not know why he survived. "Perhaps it was not my fate to die."
The eight family members include his mother and eldest daughter. His three sons and wife survived.

Tamang dreads what the future may bring, especially if these hydropower projects are shut down. "If things continue like this, we will go hungry. Sometimes I feel it would have been better not to survive."
Tamang ultimately managed to take refuge with a few others in the village of Shanti Bazar for two days until the army came to rescue them.
He estimates about 50 to 60 workers were able to escape the tunnel alongside him.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Rescue workers are operating at affected hydropower sites to try to find trapped workers

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Rescue workers are operating at affected hydropower sites to try to find trapped workers
He says more people could have been saved if proper resources had been in place.
This is echoed by a new report which says there was evidence of growing instability around the glacier in the days before the disaster - and that better early warning systems could have saved lives.

Satellite images suggest the glacier surface was moving faster, meltwater was turning brown and a crack was developing in the surrounding rock, according to experts from the Asian Mountain Academic Alliance, the Stimson Centre and China's Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment.
These are all possible signs the mountainside was becoming unstable.
The avalanche itself moved too fast for conventional warnings to help those closest to it, the scientists say.
But further downstream, where the flood took 10 minutes or more to arrive, they say a comprehensive warning system could potentially have saved a significant number of lives.

Right now, however, specialists from China, India and Nepal are continuing to use excavators and heavy machinery to blast through debris from the hydropower projects to try to reach workers still trapped at several hydropower sites.
"There are probably still some survivors inside. I would be happy if they were rescued quickly," Tamang says.
"I know many people who are still trapped there."

blocks.caption: A composite picture showing pictures from 19 July 2025 (highlighting section of glacier and mountainside which collapsed) and 27 August 2026 (showing edge of glacier after landslide)

blocks.text: Additional reporting by Justin Rowlatt, climate editor

articles.title: Magnitude 6.0 quake rocks Davao Occidental
articles.summary: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — A magnitude 6 earthquake rocked Davao Occidental at 9:22 Tuesday evening, the state volcanology office said. The tremor was tectonic in origin and was traced 115…

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — A magnitude 6 earthquake rocked Davao Occidental at 9:22 Tuesday evening, the state volcanology office said.
The tremor was tectonic in origin and was traced 115 kilometers south of Balut Island in Sarangani, Davao Occidental, according to Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs).
It has a depth of 93 kilometers.
Intensity III was felt in Don Marcelino, Jose Abad Santos, Malita, Davao Occidental; Kiamba, Sarangani: and Tupi, South Cotabato
Intensity II was recorded in Digos City, Maasim, Malapatan and Maitum in Sarangani province; Gen. Santos City and Tboli,South Cotabato.
Intensity I in Sarangani, Davao Occidental and Koronadal City.
No reported damage to properties as of posting. —EDWIN O. FERNANDEZ

articles.title: Sydney’s beaches enter the drone age to get swimmers back in the water after spate of shark attacks
articles.summary:
Seventy beaches across New South Wales are part of the $34m dawn-to-dusk drone monitoring program, which one expert has called ‘the best technology we have at the moment’

  • Get our

blocks.text: “Hey Taha, what’s the visibility like?” shouts a man with a towel slung over his shoulder.
“Uh, nice,” says Surf Life Saving New South Wales drone operator Taha Kafil-Hussain.
“Good?” the man asks. “Very good,” Kafil-Hussain assures him. Thanking him, the early morning swimmer turns and heads down the steps to Coogee beach.

Kafil-Hussain, who Guardian Australia has joined on his early morning shark surveillance flight, says: “When they’re local, they just want to see what the weather, what the water looks like, [if there’s] anything scary.”

The 22-year-old has been flying drones for SLS NSW for four years, but only at Coogee beach for a matter of weeks. Before a shark attack on 34-year-old Sydney teacher and mother Leah Stewart in June, drone surveillance was not permitted at Coogee because it lies directly under the flight path from Sydney airport’s east-west runway.

In an interview with 60 Minutes broadcast on Sunday, Stewart described the horror encounter with a four-metre white shark, after which her left arm was amputated, as “like fighting a dinosaur”. The attack, one of a series of high-profile incidents in Sydney in the past 12 months, has prompted the state government to massively ramp up its shark mitigation program.

blocks.caption: During each drone flight, Taha Kafil-Hussain rakes the bay in sections from left to right, backwards and forwards, leaving a checkerboard pattern on his control screen Photograph: Rémi Chauvin/The Guardian
Kafil-Hussain has now flown drones at most Sydney beaches, from Palm Beach in the north to Cronulla in the south. Photograph: Rémi Chauvin/The Guardian

blocks.text: Under a $34m initiative by the state government which rolled out on 1 July, 38 of Sydney’s ocean beaches, including Coogee, now receive dawn-to-dusk drone monitoring year round.

Seventy NSW beaches in total are part of the dawn-to-dusk program, while others will benefit from increased surveillance throughout the summer and school holidays. On Tuesday, surveillance hours will increase, running from 6.15am to 5pm each day for the start of spring, as daylight increases.

When Guardian Australia meets Kafil-Hussain in mid-winter, he arrives at 6.30am to throw up a marquee, before checking a radio to determine which direction the planes are flying in (drone surveillance at Coogee has been allowed with special permission from the airport).

Not long after, the drone takes off in a whir of plastic from a miniature landing pad, rising 60 metres into the air before heading out to sea. During each 20-minute flight, Kafil-Hussain rakes the bay in sections from left to right, backwards and forwards, leaving a checkerboard pattern on his control screen.
He says he’s looking for “anything moving in a different way than normal”.
“Anything moving against the flow of water, anything that looks a little bit long – anything alive, really.”
He pauses when he thinks he’s spotted something, to zoom in. “Looks like seaweed,” he says.
University of Sydney shark policy expert and associate professor Christopher Pepin-Neff agrees that “drones are the best technology that we have at the moment”.
But they say there are “important caveats that we need to give to the public”.
“On days that are windy, if the shark is too small, the drone operator is not going to be able to see a shark if it’s there.
“I’m slightly nervous that, in the absence of [a] large public education campaign, we have the possibility that we’re going to scare the shit out of people,” says Pepin-Neff.

With more drone surveillance comes more regular shark sightings. The NSW government says there have been more 750 sightings and more than 200 intervention actions by Surf Life Saving NSW since 1 July.
Shark listening stations are now tracking 1,698 white sharks, 938 tiger sharks and 374 bull sharks – the “target sharks” which are most frequently involved in serious shark bites.

Kafil-Hussain says he has seen more bull and tiger sharks than whites, and has raised the alarm a few times, most recently for a bronze whaler – involved in rare attacks – which he initially thought was a target shark.
after newsletter promotion

If it’s early and he’s on his own, raising the alarm means making the call to clear the water himself – otherwise he shares what he has seen with lifeguards and they make the decision, with the time from spotting a hazard to fully clearing the water about two or three minutes.
The SLS drones have a speaker attached to them, allowing him to communicate directly with surfers and swimmers.
It’s a technology familiar to followers of the Instagram account Drone Shark App, run by Jason Iggleden, who has been using a drone since 2018 to surveil beaches including Bondi, Tamarama and Bronte.

blocks.caption: Christopher Pepin-Neff says the drone program will ‘restore confidence’ ahead of a busy summer, but there is ‘no silver bullet’. Photograph: Steven Markham/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Videos on the account show an enormous seal barrel-rolling through the water and a swirling vortex of Australian salmon, while in another a whale lingers beneath a kayaker in Tamarama.
“I just had a bit of a vision to help … with getting people out of water with sharks, and just showing them the beauty of what’s out there,” he said.

The licensed and insured drone flyer, who continues to work independently, now passes on any sightings to SLS NSW. He is a firm believer in the drone surveillance, saying the ability to spot target sharks grows with experience.
“I don’t think you really need to consider much more than drones, to be honest,” he says.

Pepin-Neff is supportive of other non-lethal technologies, such as SMART drum lines. They say a trial of new artificial intelligence detection software on drones will take the pressure off humans to discern between more and less dangerous sharks. But their message on controversial measures like shark nets, here to stay on NSW beaches, and culling, is unequivocal: “They do not work.”
‘Not a perfect solution’

Kafil-Hussain, who drives each day from his home in Parramatta, has now flown drones at most Sydney beaches, from Palm Beach in the north to Cronulla in the south. Every beach is different – he sees turtles, dolphins, the occasional whale. Coogee is home to a wobbegong, a low-swimming carpet shark which does not hunt humans but can attack if threatened.
“He’s not around. He’ll pop out eventually,” says Kafil-Hussain.

When Guardian Australia visits the beach, arriving before sunrise, it is already heaving with eastern suburbs dog walkers, swim clubs and surfers. Just weeks after the attack on Stewart, Kafil-Hussain says numbers at the beach have only been growing.
Pepin-Neff says the drone program will “restore confidence” ahead of a busy summer, but there is “no silver bullet”. “Drones are a great tool but they’re not a perfect solution.”
Pepin-Neff swims at fully enclosed beaches, like Marrinawi Cove in Barangaroo, but their advice for those that swim at unenclosed beaches: “Swim between the flags.”
“The ocean is the wild and we need to treat the beach like the bush.”

articles.title: Pilandok intensifies into tropical storm
articles.summary: Pilandok has intensified into a tropical storm, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration reported.

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — Pilandok has intensified into a tropical storm, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration reported.

Based on the latest weather satellite at 4 p.m. yesterday, Pilandok was located 1,015 kilometers east of extreme Northern Luzon. It was packing winds of 65 kilometers per hour and gusts of up to 80 kph while moving northwestward at 10 kph.
Pilandok is expected to remain over the northern Philippine Sea before approaching Okinawa, Japan. It is expected to exit the Philippine area of responsibility later today or early tomorrow.
Meanwhile, Tropical Storm Obet was located 685 kilometers west of Calayan, Cagayan, with winds of 65 kph and gusts of up to 80 kph while moving east-northeastward at 30 kph.

Another low-pressure area was tracked 3,010 kilometers east of southeastern Luzon, moving northwestward at 15 kph. It has a medium chance of developing into a tropical cyclone within the next 24 hours.
The weather bureau said occasional rains would be experienced in Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Batanes and Zambales due to the monsoon.

Cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms are, meanwhile, expected in Metro Manila, the Cordillera Administrative Region, the rest of the Ilocos Region, the rest of Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Cavite, Batangas, Rizal, Occidental Mindoro, Aklan and Antique.

Yellow rainfall warnings, indicating 50 to 100 millimeters of rain, were raised over Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Abra, La Union, Benguet, Pangasinan, Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro from yesterday afternoon to this afternoon.

From this afternoon to Friday afternoon, an orange rainfall warning, indicating 100 to 200 mm of rain, was raised over Occidental Mindoro while yellow warnings were issued for Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga, Cavite, Batangas, Oriental Mindoro and Antique.
Disruptions
Due to the anticipated continued heavy rainfall and flooding, the Department of Foreign Affairs suspended yesterday the operations of its consular offices in Pampanga and Olongapo.

Affected applicants will be accommodated within 30 days from their original appointment date, while consular operations will resume upon further advice from the local government units with jurisdiction over the offices.
Applicants needing emergency or urgent consular services may contact the DFA Consular Offices through [email protected] and [email protected].
Sea travel was similarly disrupted. The Philippine Ports Authority said certain sea trips were canceled yesterday due to rains brought by the monsoon and tropical storm Pilandok.
In Masbate, all fastcraft operated by Montenegro Shipping Lines Inc. between Masbate City and Pilar, Sorsogon were canceled.
The MV Island Biri also canceled its 3 p.m. trip from Puerto Galera to Batangas, while Ocean Fast Ferries Inc. canceled its Maasin-Surigao trip and vice versa.
On land, floodwaters paralyzed major thoroughfares.
Motorists had been stranded for hours along the North Luzon Expressway in San Simon, Pampanga since Friday due to heavy rains, with hundreds of vehicles still stuck along the expressway as of Monday.
Cars were directed to the innermost lane while trucks and buses were allowed to use the second lane to ease traffic.
Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. ordered the deployment of more than 2,207 police officers to assist stranded motorists.
“Motorists are usually left on their own in dealing with flooded roads. We do not want that to happen. There should be police presence in areas where they are needed,” Nartatez said.
At least 12,459 personnel from reactionary standby support forces were also on standby for deployment.

In terms of infrastructure, the Department of Health reported that the damage to health facilities from the combined effects of recent tropical cyclones and the southwest monsoon had reached more than P54 million. — Rhodina Villanueva, Emmanuel Tupas, Pia Lee-Brago, Bella Cariaso

articles.title: Duterte defense team wants prosecution to ‘reframe’ charges
articles.summary: The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte wants the prosecution to “reframe” the crimes against humanity charges against him and file an updated document before the pre-trial…

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 12:00am
Former president Rodrigo Duterte
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The defense team of former president Rodrigo Duterte wants the prosecution to “reframe” the crimes against humanity charges against him and file an updated document before the pre-trial chamber of the International Criminal Court (ICC).
In an 11-page motion dated Aug. 31, defense counsel Peter Haynes said the original document containing the charges (DCC) filed by the prosecution “is not fit for purpose and should be struck out.”

According to the defense, the DCC was framed “around illustrative non-exhaustive incidents” grouped into topical headings, supposedly in violation of the former president’s right to be informed in detail of the nature, cause and content of the charges against him.

Duterte is facing charges of crimes against humanity, grouped into three sets of incidents: alleged murders in Davao from 2013 to 2016, alleged murders of high-value targets from 2016 to 2017 and alleged murders and attempted murders in relation to barangay operations from 2016 to 2018.
“The prosecution’s decision to frame the charges in this entirely novel way makes it impossible for the defendant to know what case he has to meet at trial,” read the defense’s motion.

articles.title: Marcos to lead peace consciousness month celebration
articles.summary: Acknowledging that the peace-building efforts in Mindanao is not yet finished, President Marcos yesterday vowed to ensure that the elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao…

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on January 16, 2026.
PPA Photos by Revoli Cortez

MANILA, Philippines — Acknowledging that the peace-building efforts in Mindanao is not yet finished, President Marcos yesterday vowed to ensure that the elections in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) this month would be credible and peaceful.

Speaking during the opening of the National Peace Consciousness Month at Malacañang, Marcos said the 1996 final peace deal is a landmark achievement forged through the aspirations, struggles and sacrifices of the Moro National Liberation Front and the shared resolve to build a lasting peace.
He lauded those who “chose dialogue over division” and who worked quietly and patiently to make peace a lived reality in Mindanao.
“In the coming days, we have another opportunity to show that the gains of peace can be strengthened through democratic institutions,” he said.
Marcos gave assurance that the government is prepared for the first parliamentary elections in BARMM on Sept. 14.
Marcos also vowed to continue supporting Cordillera’s aspirations for autonomy and ensure that peace continues to translate into development and opportunity.

He said the 1986 Mount Data Peace Accord with the Cordillera Bodong Administration-Cordillera People’s Liberation Army showed that even longstanding differences could be bridged through dialogue and a shared commitment to uplift communities.

articles.title: JBC invites 5 senior justices to apply for CJ position
articles.summary: Five senior justices of the Supreme Court have been “invited” to apply for the position of chief justice ahead of the retirement of Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo on Nov. 6.

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 12:00am
A hall at the Supreme Court building in Manila in an undated image.
SC PIO
MANILA, Philippines — Five senior justices of the Supreme Court have been “invited” to apply for the position of chief justice ahead of the retirement of Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo on Nov. 6.

“The Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) has invited the five most senior associate justices of the Supreme Court… to apply for the vacancy that will arise upon the retirement of Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo,” SC spokesperson Camille Sue Mae Ting said in a statement yesterday.
The five justices invited were Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen and Associate Justices Alfredo Benjamin Caguioa, Ramon Paul Hernando, Henri Jean Paul Inting and Rodil Zalameda.

“Since the early 2000s, the JBC has followed the practice of inviting the five most senior Associate Justices to apply for the Chief Justice post as a matter of courtesy and in recognition of their seniority,” Ting said.

Leonen was appointed to the SC in November 2012, making him the most senior among the SC justices. Caguioa entered the high court in January 2016, Hernando in October 2018, Inting in February 2019 and Zalameda in August 2019.

Associate Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier, who was supposedly more senior than Zalameda, having been appointed in March 2019, is set to retire in November when she reaches the retirement age of 70. Meanwhile, the remaining eight justices were appointed between January 2020 and June 2025.

articles.title: P37.49 billion ‘pork barrel’ for LGUs flagged
articles.summary: Makabayan lawmakers have condemned the Marcos administration for its handling of the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, saying it still reeks of pork barrel funds allotted to local…

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Makabayan lawmakers have condemned the Marcos administration for its handling of the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027, saying it still reeks of pork barrel funds allotted to local government units.

Rep. Antonio Tinio has criticized the administration’s “brazen distribution” of special allotment release orders (SAROs) to local officials, flagging a P37.49-billion hike in alleged pork barrel funds under the Local Government Support Fund (LGSF).
He said this can be found in the financial assistance to local government units (LGUs) under the 2026 General Appropriations Act, which had “ballooned” to such a “staggering amount.”
The original 2026 National Expenditure Program (NEP) only contained P5 billion for such item, he pointed out.

“At the time, we called this LGU pork. The total LGSF for 2026 reached P68 billion, far higher than the original proposal from the executive. Why did it balloon to P37.49 billion for Financial Assistance to LGUs, when it was just P5 billion in the NEP?” Tinio said.

“It is true that the 2027 budget is flooded with pork barrel funds. Now, they also have SARO pork barrel giveaways too. Clearly, this is a vehicle for congressional insertions and the patronage politics that come with it,” he added.

But the League of Municipalities of the Philippines (LMP) assured the public that “strict safeguards” are in place to keep the proposed P58.32-billion LGSF for 2027 free from political favoritism, ensuring that LGUs get their fair share.
The amount is so far the biggest LGSF budget allocation in Philippine history, according to LMP national president and Echague, Isabela Mayor Faustino Dy V.
Rules set by the Department of Budget and Management should ensure that LGUs receive their fair share regardless of political affiliation, Dy said.
OP budget quickly approved
Citing institutional and inter-branch courtesy, the House appropriations committee has swiftly approved the Office of the President (OP)’s proposed P10.15-billion budget for 2027.
Of the amount, about P4.5 billion is for confidential and intelligence expenses.

Executive Secretary Ralph Recto explained that the OP’s proposed budget is 64 percent lower than its 2026 budget, citing lower operational requirements of its delivery units and the completion of activities related to the country’s hosting of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit.
Tinio had argued that the OP should explain why almost half of its budget proposal is for confidential funds.
The House panel approved the budget and terminated further discussions and interpellations in less than 20 minutes.
DA eyes lower budget

The Department of Agriculture (DA) is seeking a lower overall budget for 2027, with allocations for farm-to-market roads (FMRs) seeing a P17-billion cut but giving larger share for locally funded and foreign-assisted projects despite a history of weak program spending, a budget watchdog warned.

Based on the 2027 NEP, the DA’s budget is set to fall by nearly eight percent, to P171.32 billion from P185.77 billion under the 2026 General Appropriations Act, even as food security and rising farm-input costs remain key concerns.
But People’s Budget Coalition co-convenor AJ Montesa called for attention on the lower FMR allocation and growing locally funded and foreign-assisted project portfolio.
The FMR budget was slashed to P16 billion from P33 billion in 2026.

Montesa noted that the DA’s locally funded and foreign-assisted program secured P76.87 billion for 2027, a P5.3-billion increase from P71.61 billion this year, even as the projects have historically posted weak spending rates.

Timothy Salomon, program officer at Task Force Mapalad – a national federation of farmers, farm workers and advocates – questioned the need for the DA to source nearly half of its program budget from foreign-assisted projects.
Salomon called on Congress to “remove all pork barrels, put the people’s money where the President’s mouth is.”

Most of the agencies attached to the DA are facing budget cuts. The Philippine Carabao Center’s budget fell by nearly 34 percent, to P1.37 billion. The National Meat Inspection Service slipped by 48.9 percent, to P346.25 million.
The Agricultural Credit Policy Council went down by 8.1 percent, to P2.86 billion. The Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority was cut by 37.6 percent, to P264.03 million.
However, the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources’ proposed budget grew by 4.1 percent, to P12.25 billion from P11.76 billion this year. — Daphne Galvez, Aubrey Rose Inosante

articles.title: PNP tightens security at pumping stations
articles.summary: Police have tightened security at flood control facilities in Metro Manila following reports of theft of parts and equipment that disrupted operations amid strong monsoon rains last week.

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 12:00am

Philippine Coast Guard personnel help secure the Sunog Apog Pumping Station in Tondo, Manila on September 1, 2026, following reports of stolen specialized equipment and other components vital to the facility’s flood control operations.
Noel Pabalate

MANILA, Philippines — Police have tightened security at flood control facilities in Metro Manila following reports of theft of parts and equipment that disrupted operations amid strong monsoon rains last week.

“I have directed concerned police units to coordinate with local governments and facility operators, intensify security and conduct immediate investigations to identify and arrest those responsible,” Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said.
Stolen cables, valves and manhole covers impaired operations of flood mitigation facilities in the capital, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon revealed earlier.
Thieves stole high-voltage cables at the Sunog Apog facility in Manila, grounding cables at the Navotas pumping station and heavy-duty check valves at the Tumana pumping station in Marikina.
Manhole covers along Roxas Boulevard were also missing.
Replacing the stolen components would cost public funds, Nartatez stressed.
“Those who steal or buy stolen equipment will be held accountable under the law. We will pursue the perpetrators and ensure that appropriate charges are filed against them,” Nartatez said.
Probe infrastructure damage
Sen. Vicente Sotto III has filed a resolution seeking a probe on the recent spate of typhoons and floods to strengthen the country’s disaster response.
In Senate Resolution 631, Sotto cited reports of about P5.1 billion in damage to infrastructure, including the collapse of several roads, bridges and flood control facilities.
Sotto expressed concern over the Department of Health’s tally of at least 5,486 leptospirosis cases, as well as reports of fatalities due to the flooding.
Sotto stressed the need to assess the resilience of public infrastructure amid worsening typhoons due to climate change.
Meanwhile, Antipolo Bishop Ruperto Cruz Santos said relentless flooding caused by negligence and corruption is a crime against God and the people. — Marc Jayson Cayabyab, Bella Cariaso

articles.title: AMLC: Freeze order issued vs lawmaker’s assets
articles.summary: The Anti-Money Laundering Council has secured a Court of Appeals order freezing 55 bank accounts and four insurance policies tied to an unnamed lawmaker associated with government projects worth…

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 12:00am
This photo shows the Anti-Money Laundering Council seal.
Philstar.com illustration

MANILA, Philippines — The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) has secured a Court of Appeals order freezing 55 bank accounts and four insurance policies tied to an unnamed lawmaker associated with government projects worth billions of pesos.
In a statement, the AMLC said the freeze order also covered the assets of a construction company linked to the legislator and associated individuals.
The appellate court issued the order on Aug. 25 after finding probable cause that the assets were connected to violations of Republic Act 3019, or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.

A freeze order is a temporary measure intended to prevent assets suspected of being linked to unlawful activities from being used, transferred or disposed of while authorities pursue their case. It does not constitute a final forfeiture of the assets.
Under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, the Court of Appeals may issue a freeze order upon a verified petition by the AMLC and a finding of probable cause.
The order may remain in effect for a period determined by the court but not exceeding six months if no case is filed against the account holder.

The AMLC said the case stemmed from investigations conducted by the Office of the Ombudsman and the Bureau of Internal Revenue, along with a separate administrative inquiry by the House of Representatives.
The lawmaker had claimed that he divested his interest in the construction business before assuming public office.

However, records showed that the legislator continued receiving proceeds from the business while serving in government, according to the AMLC. The agency said this indicated that he continued exercising control over the construction companies.

The AMLC did not identify the lawmaker, the construction company or the other individuals covered by the order. It also did not disclose the value of the frozen assets or provide a breakdown of their ownership.

articles.title: DBM Oks P10.38 billion for zero balance billing
articles.summary: The Department of Budget and Management has approved the release of P10.38 billion to support the implementation of the Zero Balance Billing program, aimed at easing the financial burden of…

blocks.text: September 2, 2026 | 12:00am
A nurse monitors newborns at the nursery of the East Avenue Medical Center in Quezon City in this file photo from August 2025. The hospital implements the government’s zero-balance billing policy.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) has approved the release of P10.38 billion to support the implementation of the Zero Balance Billing (ZBB) program, aimed at easing the financial burden of hospitalization and improving access to health care.
In a statement, the DBM said that the approved funding will support the rollout of ZBB in DOH hospitals nationwide and six pilot local government unit (LGU) hospitals.

“No Filipino should have to choose between getting the medical care they need and protecting their family from a hospital bill they cannot afford. This P10.377-billion release is about making sure that when our people get sick, the government is there to help carry the burden,” Acting Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon said.
Of the total, P9.38 billion will support ZBB in 12 DOH hospitals in Metro Manila.

This allocation covers DOH hospitals including Amang Rodriguez Memorial Medical Center, Dr. Jose Fabella Memorial Hospital, East Avenue Medical Center, Jose R. Reyes Memorial Medical Center, National Center for Mental Health, National Children’s Hospital, Philippine Orthopedic Center, Quirino Memorial Medical Center, Research Institute for Tropical Medicine, Rizal Medical Center, San Lazaro Hospital and Tondo Medical Center.
The remaining allocation of P6.04 billion will support the implementation of ZBB in DOH regional hospitals and other government health facilities outside Metro Manila.
The DBM also downloaded P1 billion to support the implementation of the ZBB Program in six pilot LGU hospitals in Benguet, Batangas, Laguna, Quezon, Aklan and Sarangani.
“The funding expands the reach of the program beyond DOH-run hospitals and brings government support closer to patients seeking treatment in their own provinces and communities,” the agency said.
The approved funding is chargeable against the DOH budget under the 2026 General Appropriations Act.

The ZBB program is part of the government’s broader efforts to advance Universal Health Care by helping ensure that eligible patients admitted to participating government hospitals can receive covered health services with minimal or no remaining hospital bill, subject to applicable guidelines and eligibility requirements.

articles.title: Thinking of leaving your desk job and entering the trades? Here's your guide
articles.summary: After more than 25 years into his job as a business administrator, Simon Hardcastle felt there was nothing left for him to learn, so he signed up to drive a skid steer to plow snow. It was a…

image.caption: A steel worker welds a new staircase at a construction site on Thursday, June 27, 2024. (Sean Kilpatrick/Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Hamilton

After more than 25 years into his job as a business administrator, Simon Hardcastle felt there was nothing left for him to learn, so he signed up to drive a skid steer to plow snow. It was a financial risk, but a lot more fun.
Some career counsellors say they see more mid-career workers wanting to switch to skilled trades
More than 25 years into his job as a business administrator, Simon Hardcastle felt there was nothing left for him to learn.
He didn't hate his job, but it wasn't thrilling either, Hardcastle recalled.
Then, one day at work, he signed up to drive a skid steer to plow snow, and he knew it was time for a shakeup.

"I moved snow, and about two hours later I thought, 'Wow, this is really good fun! What else can I do?" the 49-year-old Ancaster, Ont., resident said. "So, I spoke to my wife and I was like, 'I'm thinking of changing careers."'

items: 1,200 National Steel Car workers in Hamilton on strike after rejecting contract offer
9 Hamilton businesses affected by Trump tariffs will get $12.5M in federal funding

blocks.text: He knew going from a desk job to a skilled trade wasn't going to be easy. It meant giving up a stable paycheque for a while, and temporarily transitioning to a single-income household while also raising two kids.
But he was sure that's what he wanted to do.

For many Canadians, skilled trades have started to become more attractive as a career option, partly as various levels of government invest heavily in these professions while a boom in artificial intelligence creates fear over the future of many desk jobs.
Some career counsellors say they're seeing more interest among mid-career workers to make a switch. However, not knowing where to begin often delays the process.
Start by understanding the different trade opportunities, said Rachel Buesink, general manager at Express Employment Professionals in Hamilton.
Online assessment tools can help you figure out where your strengths lie — whether that's building things, mathematics and problem-solving, or even general handyman work, she said.
But just having an interest isn't enough.
Buesink said a lot of times, people come to her with misconceptions.
"So many people come in and say: 'I've hung pictures, I can build anything from Ikea, I want to be a carpenter,"' she said.

But many don't realize how lengthy and demanding the journey is, she said. It can take four years of school and several exams. You also need an employer who can document your progress and is willing to hire you as an apprentice.
It takes time to get to a well-paid job, expert says
Shelley Gray, chief executive officer of SkilledTradesBC, says exposure to your desired job or industry can help cement that decision.
Gray said several institutions offer sampler or pre-apprenticeship programs to try out various trades. That could also be a help in getting into a full-time program or finding an employer, she said.

items: Oshawa plant adds truck as unionized Canadian GM members ratify new deals
Canada launches alliance to tackle advanced manufacturing workforce shortages

blocks.text: Buesink said switching careers is about "looking at understanding what each skilled trade opportunity is, trying to best match it with your strengths and interest, and then trying to keep up with the ever-changing economic demands for that trade.
"It is a bit of a balancing act."
Keeping up with bills and supporting a family during the transition can also be a challenge.
"The biggest thing is the wage cut until you're trained and able to add value to the company," Buesink said.
She said workers in transition can get employment insurance or make some money from apprenticeships. But overall, it takes time to get to a well-paid job.
'It's so much fun, like, I can't even explain'
For Hardcastle, switching to operating heavy equipment was a calculated financial risk.
He and his wife saved up for a couple of months before he could finally quit his day job, and he took out a loan for his certification.
Getting certified is crucial to landing a well-paying job. But that could take time, depending on the program you choose.
For example, it can take about four months to become a truck driver, a year to become a welder and five years to become a qualified electrician.
Gray said many skilled trades offer a level of flexibility to apprentices to learn at their own pace.
But she said it's crucial to find an employer who can sponsor you. "Eighty per cent of apprenticeship happens in the workplace."

College programs with co-ops can help with placements in most cases, Buesink said. But if there aren't enough spots, she said this is where your previous desk job could help boost your resume and show your eagerness to work.

"If you have a strong resume, if you have a good background and a willingness (that shows): 'Hey, I'm in school, this is what I want to do,' — that makes you more attractive to the potential employer," she said.
While it can take a while to get trained, Gray said she often hears from people about high levels of job satisfaction alongside good pay.
That's true in Hardcastle's case. He didn't have to take a pay cut and now gets to do something that excites him.
"Right now, it's like a kid in a sandbox," he said. "I'm playing with these big machines and I'm moving material.
"Every day is different. It's so much fun, like, I can't even explain."

articles.title: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack
articles.summary: A drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at the airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes on 4 August.

blocks.text: Germany has said Russia was responsible for last month's drone attack at Leipzig's airport.
A drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany, close to Ukrainian cargo planes, on 4 August.

It failed to explode as the detonator was apparently faulty, and investigators suspect a second drone collided with a cargo aircraft nearby. A third drone was reportedly found near the airport 10 days later.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the Leipzig airport attack followed the "well-established pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe" and the assumption was that Germany would be targeted again.
Security experts had speculated that Russia may have been responsible, however Russia has always rejected claims of involvement.

Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany is used by the Germany military and Nato allies for the transport of military goods and also serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines - which carries most of the country's aerial cargo.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, who was standing beside Dobrindt at a press conference in Berlin, said he would order the closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn, and the contract for the Russian House in Berlin will also be terminated - which many observers have said has been used for espionage and to spread Russian propaganda.
The head of Nato, Mark Rutte, said the organisation "stands in full solidarity with Germany".
"The evidence is clear. And I welcome the measures announced by Germany in response," he wrote on X.
The issue will be discussed at a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Ireland later on Tuesday.
